1	---
2	title: "Tools: media"
3	description: The agent tools that bring files into a project, relink and remove them, copy them into the package, and set a file's Camera Log, peak and speech.
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	These tools work on the project's media list, the files a project points at. A file on the list isn't on the timeline until a clip uses it. See [Tools: adding clips](/mcp/tools-adding-clips/).
9	
10	<AtAGlance
11	  tools={['import_media', 'add_media', 'relink_media', 'remove_media', 'consolidate_media', 'set_media_color', 'set_media_speech']}
12	/>
13	
14	The media list belongs to the whole project, not to a nest, so:
15	
16	- Pass `scope` to `add_media`, `relink_media`, `remove_media`, `set_media_color` or `set_media_speech`, and Frame Job answers that the edit has no meaning inside a nest.
17	- With a nest open and no `scope` passed, those same edits apply to the whole project. All but `add_media` name themselves under `document_ops` in the answer.
18	- Media ids mean the same thing everywhere.
19	
20	Every tool here also takes an optional `project`, the path of an open project as `get_project` reports it. Without it the call goes to the frontmost project. Each edit is one undo step. See [What a call answers](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/) for the `project` summary and the two ways an edit can fail to happen.
21	
22	## `import_media`
23	
24	Reads a movie, sound file, picture or `.cube` LUT and adds it to the media list, as [**File ▸ Add Media…**](/projects/import-media/#add-media) does. It isn't on the timeline yet. Place it with [`add_clip`](/mcp/tools-adding-clips/).
25	
26	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
27	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
28	| `path` | string | Yes | The file, as an absolute path or one starting with `~`. |
29	| `project` | string | No | The project to add it to. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
30	
31	It answers:
32	
33	| Key | What it is |
34	| --- | --- |
35	| `media` | The new media id. |
36	| `path` | Where the entry points. For a converted file, that's the copy. |
37	| `original` | The file you named, when the entry points at a copy. |
38	| `kind` | `video`, `audio`, `image` or `lut`. |
39	| `duration` | The file's length, in ticks. |
40	| `width`, `height` | Its display size. |
41	| `fps` | Its frame rate, as `[numerator, denominator]`. |
42	| `has_video`, `has_audio`, `has_alpha` | What it holds. |
43	| `note` | What to do next: `add_clip`, or for a LUT, [`set_video`](/mcp/tools-set-video/) with a look. |
44	| `project` | The `project` summary. |
45	
46	A [WebM or Matroska file](/projects/webm-and-matroska/) is copied into a `.mov` first and named after the original. A file the [ffmpeg step](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/) converts is recorded the same way.
47	
48	A tool call never asks, so where the app would offer to convert a file with ffmpeg, this answers with the reason instead. Convert it from the app's window, or set Frame Job to always convert.
49	
50	It's refused when nothing exists at `path`, or when the file can't be read. A file whose path is already on the list changes nothing, and the answer says so. The step is called "Add Media".
51	
52	## `add_media`
53	
54	Adds a media entry from a description you supply, with no reading of the file. Use `import_media` unless you're replaying a project's own JSON. Frame Job has no menu item for this tool, because reading the file is the app's job.
55	
56	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
57	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
58	| `descriptor` | object | Yes | The entry to add, as below. |
59	| `scope` | integer | No | Answers that this has no meaning inside a nest. |
60	| `project` | string | No | The project to add it to. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
61	
62	The descriptor is an element of `media` from `get_project`, without its `id`. Only `path` is required by name.
63	
64	| Key | What it is | Default |
65	| --- | --- | --- |
66	| `path` | The file. A leading `~` is expanded. | |
67	| `bookmark` | A base64 security bookmark. | None |
68	| `kind` | `video`, `audio`, `image` or `lut`. | `video` |
69	| `duration` | The length, in ticks. | 0 |
70	| `width`, `height` | The size in pixels. A file with pixels needs both. | 0 |
71	| `fps` | The frame rate, as `[numerator, denominator]`. | `[30, 1]` |
72	| `has_video` | Whether it has a picture. | On for `video` and `image` |
73	| `has_audio` | Whether it has sound. | On for `audio` |
74	| `has_alpha` | Whether it has an alpha channel. | Off |
75	| `original` | `{path, bookmark?}`: the file a `.mov` copy or conversion was made from. | None |
76	| `color` | A video file's Camera Log, as `set_media_color` takes it, plus `detected`, and `pq`, a PQ file's `{file?, from?, peak?}` as `get_project` shows it. | None |
77	| `cursor` | `{path, bookmark?, in_picture}`: the cursor file recorded beside a video, with `in_picture` true when the movie's own picture already shows the pointer. Both `path` and `in_picture` are required, and it's for a video with a picture only. | None |
78	
79	It answers `ok: true`, `media` (the new id), `path` and the `project` summary.
80	
81	An unknown key is refused by name, and so is a value of the wrong shape. A picture with no width or height, a video with a frame-rate term of 0, an empty path and a negative duration are all refused. A `color` that `set_media_color` wouldn't take is refused too. A path already on the list changes nothing.
82	
83	## `relink_media`
84	
85	Points a media entry at a file that moved, as [the Relink… sheet](/projects/relink-media/) and the Media tab's row menu do. `get_project`'s `missing_media` names the entries that need this.
86	
87	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
88	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
89	| `media` | integer | Yes | The media id. |
90	| `path` | string | Yes | Where the file is now. |
91	| `bookmark` | string | No | A base64 security bookmark. Leave it out and one is made for you, so the next move is followed automatically. |
92	| `scope` | integer | No | Answers that this has no meaning inside a nest. |
93	| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
94	
95	The new file is read as `import_media` reads one, and the entry takes its duration, size, frame rate and audio, video and alpha flags. What happens to the rest is on [Relink missing media](/projects/relink-media/#what-a-relink-keeps):
96	
97	- A clip running past the end of a shorter file is shortened to end with it. One that starts past the new end keeps a single frame.
98	- Camera Log and an HDR10 peak are kept.
99	- Saved speech is held to the new file, and forgotten when the new file has no sound.
100	- The cursor file beside the new movie is taken. If there's none, the old one stays as long as it's still there and the new movie is the same size. Otherwise the entry's cursor file is cleared.
101	- A WebM or Matroska file is copied into a `.mov` first, and a file the ffmpeg step converts is recorded the same way. Either becomes the entry's new `original`, and any other file clears it.
102	
103	It answers `ok: true`, `media`, `path`, `kind`, `duration`, `width`, `height`, `fps`, `has_video`, `has_audio`, `has_alpha`, `original` when there is one, and the `project` summary.
104	
105	It's refused when no media has that id, when nothing exists at `path`, when the file can't be read, and for a file of another kind, such as a sound file for a video entry. The step is called "Relink Media".
106	
107	## `remove_media`
108	
109	Removes a media entry from the project, as [**Remove** in the Media tab's row menu](/projects/remove-media/) does. The file on disk isn't touched.
110	
111	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
112	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
113	| `media` | integer | Yes | The media id. |
114	| `with_clips` | boolean | No | Remove the clips using it as well, including those inside nests. For a LUT, clear the looks and Camera Log conversions that name it instead. Default `false`. |
115	| `scope` | integer | No | Answers that this has no meaning inside a nest. |
116	| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
117	
118	A nest clip isn't a user of the file, so it stays even when clips inside it go. Any [Hide While Silent](/effects/hide-while-silent/) setting that listens to the file is cleared.
119	
120	It answers `ok: true`, `media` and the `project` summary.
121	
122	It's refused while clips use the file and `with_clips` isn't `true`, naming the clips. A LUT in use as a look or a Camera Log is refused the same way, naming what uses it. The step is called "Remove Media".
123	
124	## `consolidate_media`
125	
126	Copies every file the project references into `media/` inside the `.framejob` package and relinks the project at the copies, as [**File ▸ Consolidate Media…**](/projects/consolidate-media/) does. Afterwards the package is the whole edit. It can be moved or archived and still open with the original footage deleted.
127	
128	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
129	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
130	| `project` | string | No | The project to consolidate. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
131	
132	It copies as many bytes as the footage weighs, so it can take a while, and it has no **Cancel**. Frame Job's window doesn't respond until it's done. A recording's cursor file is copied beside its movie.
133	
134	Files already inside are left alone, and missing files are reported rather than guessed at. A file that can't be copied keeps pointing at the original, so the project always still opens.
135	
136	It answers `ok: true`, `copied`, `bytes`, `directory`, `summary`, `failures` and `missing` when there are any, and the `project` summary. When every file it can find is already inside, it answers `copied: 0`, `directory`, `missing`, a `note`, and the summary, and makes no step.
137	
138	It's refused when the project has never been saved, so call `save_project` with a path first, when the project references no media files, and when nothing could be copied. The step is called "Consolidate Media".
139	
140	The [Assistant](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/) asks you first.
141	
142	## `set_media_color`
143	
144	Sets how a video file's camera log footage is converted to Rec. 709, as the Media tab's [Camera Log popup](/hdr/camera-log/) does, and where a PQ file's highlights roll off to white, as its [HDR10 Peak field](/hdr/hdr10-peak/) does.
145	
146	Every clip of the file and its reverse follow the setting. It's converted before the chroma key and every grade, and [Show Ungraded](/color/show-ungraded/) keeps it.
147	
148	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
149	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
150	| `media` | integer | Yes | The video's media id, or a PQ still's for `peak` alone. |
151	| `color` | object or null | Yes | What to set, as below. `null` clears it, but the key must be there. |
152	| `scope` | integer | No | Answers that this has no meaning inside a nest. |
153	| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
154	
155	`color` is one of these:
156	
157	| `color` | What it does |
158	| --- | --- |
159	| `{log, gamut?}` | Converts with a built-in curve. |
160	| `{lut}` | Converts with an imported `.cube`, named by its media id. [`import_media`](#import_media) it first. See [Camera log from your own LUT](/hdr/log-luts/). |
161	| `{peak}` | A PQ file's peak, a whole number of cd/m² from 1 to 10,000. |
162	| `log` or `lut` beside `peak` | Both at once. |
163	| `null` | No conversion, which shows the log picture, and no peak override. |
164	
165	The curves, and the gamuts each takes. An absent `gamut` means the first one listed:
166	
167	| `log` | The curve | `gamut` |
168	| --- | --- | --- |
169	| `apple_log` | Apple Log | `bt2020` |
170	| `apple_log2` | Apple Log 2 | `apple_wide_gamut` |
171	| `slog3` | S-Log3 | `s_gamut3_cine`, `s_gamut3` |
172	| `vlog` | V-Log | `v_gamut` |
173	| `canon_log2` | Canon Log 2 | `cinema_gamut`, `bt2020` |
174	| `canon_log3` | Canon Log 3 | `cinema_gamut`, `bt2020` |
175	
176	An Apple Log or Apple Log 2 file is set at import, and `get_project` shows `detected: true` in the file's `media[].color`.
177	
178	Import reads a PQ file's own peak into `media[].color.pq`, as `{file, from}`: MaxCLL, or else the mastering display's maximum. When the file names neither, `pq` is `{}`, which means 1,000. `peak` overrides that reading.
179	
180	:::caution
181	`color` replaces the Camera Log and the peak together, so send both to keep both. `null` clears both, and the peak goes back to the file's own reading.
182	:::
183	
184	It answers `ok: true`, `media` and the `project` summary. The step is called "PQ Peak" when `color` holds only `peak`, and "Camera Log" otherwise.
185	
186	It's refused:
187	
188	- on an audio file or a LUT
189	- on a picture, unless it's a PQ still and `color` is `peak` alone
190	- for a `peak` on a file that isn't PQ, or outside 1 to 10,000
191	- for a `color` with none of `log`, `lut` and `peak`
192	- for `log` and `lut` together
193	- for a `gamut` without a `log`, or one its curve doesn't take
194	- for a `lut` that doesn't name a LUT in the project
195	- for `detected` or `pq`, which only import writes
196	
197	## `set_media_speech`
198	
199	Saves where a file's speech is. [Duck by Speech](/audio/duck-by-speech/#where-the-speech-comes-from) ducks the mix by these spans, and [Hide While Silent](/effects/hide-while-silent/) reads them too.
200	
201	**Audio ▸ Ducking ▸ Duck by Speech** writes them from the file's detected speech, and so does [`set_audio`](/mcp/tools-set-audio/) with `duck.mode` set to speech. Call this only to give spans of your own.
202	
203	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
204	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
205	| `media` | integer | Yes | The media id. |
206	| `spans` | array of `[start, end]` pairs | Yes | Where the speech is, in ticks of the file played forward, sorted, with each end excluded. An empty list means the file has no speech. |
207	| `scope` | integer | No | Answers that this has no meaning inside a nest. |
208	| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
209	
210	It answers `ok: true`, `media` and the `project` summary, and `get_project` shows the spans as `media[].speech`. Spans equal to what the file already has change nothing. The step is called "Speech Spans".
211	
212	It's refused:
213	
214	- on a file with no sound
215	- for a span that starts before 0, ends at or before its start, or ends past the file's duration
216	- for spans out of order or overlapping. Touching is fine.
217	- past 100,000 spans
218

1	---
2	title: "Tools: adding clips"
3	description: The agent tools that place media, titles, shapes, adjustment clips and backgrounds on the timeline, with every argument, answer and refusal.
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	These tools put new clips on the timeline. Three place a media file, three make a clip with no source, and two make a backdrop on a new track of its own.
9	
10	<AtAGlance
11	  tools={['add_clip', 'insert_clip', 'overwrite_clip', 'add_text_clip', 'add_shape_clip', 'add_adjustment_clip', 'add_background', 'add_blurred_background']}
12	/>
13	
14	## What the tools share
15	
16	Each one is one undo step. It answers `ok: true`, `new_clips` (the ids it made), `new_tracks` when it made a track, and the `project` summary. See [What a call answers](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/).
17	
18	Times and lengths are ticks, 600,000 per second, rounded to the project's frame grid. A negative `at` is taken as 0. Colours are four numbers, `[r, g, b, a]`, each from 0 to 1. See [Units and ids](/mcp/units-and-ids/).
19	
20	**`project`** is the path of an open project as `get_project` reports it. Without it the call goes to the frontmost project.
21	
22	**`scope`** is a nest id. With it, the call's ids and times are looked up inside that nest. Without it, the call goes wherever the app is looking. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/).
23	
24	**The overlap rule** stops a placement that breaks it. A clip may overlap at most one neighbour on each side, and each overlap may be at most half of the shorter clip, because an overlap is a transition. A new clip that overlaps the clip before it and has no transition gets a cross dissolve.
25	
26	**A locked track** doesn't stop these tools, apart from `insert_clip`. Locks hold back gestures in the window and what a timeline-wide shift may touch.
27	
28	## `add_clip`
29	
30	Places a whole media file as one clip, as [dragging a Media-tab row onto a track](/editing/add-clips/#drag-media-onto-a-track) does.
31	
32	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
33	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
34	| `track` | integer | Yes | The track id. `get_project` lists them. |
35	| `media` | integer | Yes | The media id. `import_media` returns one. |
36	| `at` | integer | Yes | Where the clip starts on the timeline, in ticks. |
37	| `scope` | integer | No | The nest to place it in. |
38	| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. |
39	
40	The clip starts at source time 0 and runs the media's whole length, rounded down to whole frames so it never outruns the file. Trim it afterwards with [`trim_start`](/mcp/tools-move-and-trim/#trim_start) and [`trim_end`](/mcp/tools-move-and-trim/#trim_end). A picture with no length of its own runs 5 seconds.
41	
42	It's given Fit scale when the project's `fit_new_clips` is on, which it is by default, and the source is bigger than the canvas.
43	
44	It's refused when it would break the overlap rule. A media shorter than a frame or with no duration can't be placed, and neither can a LUT, which is applied as a [look](/mcp/tools-set-video/). The step is called "Add Clip".
45	
46	## `insert_clip`
47	
48	The insert edit, as [**Edit ▸ Insert at Playhead**](/editing/insert-and-overwrite/#insert-a-file) or <kbd>⌥</kbd>-dropping a Media-tab row does. It makes room for the whole media at `at`, so nothing is covered.
49	
50	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
51	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
52	| `track` | integer | Yes | The track id. |
53	| `media` | integer | Yes | The media id. |
54	| `at` | integer | Yes | Where to insert, in ticks. |
55	| `scope` | integer | No | The nest to insert in. |
56	| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. |
57	
58	In one step:
59	
60	1. The clip `at` falls inside on `track` is split.
61	2. Every unlocked track opens by the media's length. Clips starting at or after `at` move later, and so do markers at or after it.
62	3. The media lands in the hole.
63	
64	Only the destination track is cut. A clip straddling `at` on another track stays whole, which is what keeps a music bed unbroken. The exception is a cut clip's linked partner on an unlocked track, which is cut at `at` too and paired with it.
65	
66	It's refused when `track` is locked, because the room can't be made there, and when a step of the edit is refused, in that step's own words. A media `add_clip` can't place can't be inserted either. The step is called "Insert".
67	
68	## `overwrite_clip`
69	
70	The overwrite edit, as [**Edit ▸ Overwrite at Playhead**](/editing/insert-and-overwrite/#overwrite-with-a-file) or <kbd>⇧⌥</kbd>-dropping a Media-tab row does. It takes the room instead of making it.
71	
72	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
73	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
74	| `track` | integer | Yes | The track id. |
75	| `media` | integer | Yes | The media id. |
76	| `at` | integer | Yes | Where to overwrite, in ticks. |
77	| `scope` | integer | No | The nest to overwrite in. |
78	| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. |
79	
80	The span the media needs is cleared on `track` alone: cut at both ends, and whatever is left inside removed. Nothing shifts, so the cut's length and every other track stay as they are.
81	
82	The exception is a cut clip's linked partner on an unlocked track, which is cut at the same bounds and paired. The partner's middle piece stays, unlinked.
83	
84	The named track is cleared even when it's locked. It's refused when the clip can't be placed once the span is clear, and a media `add_clip` can't place can't be used here either. The step is called "Overwrite".
85	
86	## `add_text_clip`
87	
88	Adds a text clip, a title, as the [**Add Text**](/text-and-shapes/text-clips/#add-a-text-clip) button does. It has no source, so it can be any length. Style it afterwards with `set_text` and place it with `set_video`.
89	
90	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
91	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
92	| `track` | integer | Yes | The track id. |
93	| `at` | integer | Yes | Where it starts, in ticks. |
94	| `duration` | integer | No | Its length, in ticks. Default 5 seconds (`3000000`). |
95	| `text` | object or string | No | A plain string is the words. An object is a `set_text` patch merged over the Title preset. Default: the preset's own placeholder, "Title". |
96	| `scope` | integer | No | The nest to add it in. |
97	| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. |
98	
99	A new clip is the Title preset: 72 px white Source Sans 3 Bold, centred. An object can set anything [`set_text`](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/) can, including `content`, `font`, `size`, `color`, `align`, `valign`, `outline`, `backdrop`, `width`, `animation`, `case`, `words` and `word_style`. See [Patches](/mcp/patches/).
100	
101	```json
102	{ "track": 3, "at": 1800000, "text": "Chapter one" }
103	{ "track": 3, "at": 1800000, "duration": 1200000,
104	  "text": { "content": "Chapter one", "size": 96, "align": "left" } }
105	```
106	
107	It's refused for a duration under one frame, for an unknown key or a bad value in the patch, by name, and when it would break the overlap rule. The step is called "Add Text".
108	
109	## `add_shape_clip`
110	
111	Adds a rectangle, ellipse, line or arrow drawn over the video, as [**Add Shape**](/text-and-shapes/shape-clips/#add-a-shape-clip) does. Like text, it has no source and can be any length. [`set_shape`](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/) changes it afterwards and `set_video` places it.
112	
113	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
114	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
115	| `track` | integer | Yes | The track id. |
116	| `at` | integer | Yes | Where it starts, in ticks. |
117	| `duration` | integer | No | Its length, in ticks. Default 5 seconds (`3000000`). |
118	| `shape` | object or string | No | A plain string is a kind: `rectangle`, `ellipse`, `line` or `arrow`. An object is a `set_shape` patch merged over the default rectangle. |
119	| `scope` | integer | No | The nest to add it in. |
120	| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. |
121	
122	Leave out `shape` for the default: a 320×120 rectangle, outlined with no fill. An object can set `kind`, `width`, `height`, `stroke`, `fill`, `radius`, `arrow_start`, `arrow_end`, `from`, `to` and `gradient`.
123	
124	A rounded rectangle is a rectangle with a `radius`, not a kind of its own. An arrow is created with its head on, so pass `arrow_end: false` for a bare diagonal. A box bigger than the canvas gets Fit scale when `fit_new_clips` is on, as oversized footage does.
125	
126	It's refused for a duration under one frame, for an unknown kind, key or value, by name, and when it would break the overlap rule. The step is called "Add Shape".
127	
128	## `add_adjustment_clip`
129	
130	Adds an adjustment clip, as [**Insert ▸ Adjustment Clip**](/color/adjustment-clips/#insert-an-adjustment-clip) does. It has no picture of its own. While it lasts, it grades everything drawn behind it: every lower track and the canvas background, never a track in front.
131	
132	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
133	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
134	| `track` | integer | Yes | The track id. |
135	| `at` | integer | Yes | Where it starts, in ticks. |
136	| `duration` | integer | No | Its length, in ticks. Default 5 seconds (`3000000`). |
137	| `scope` | integer | No | Answers that this has no meaning inside a nest. |
138	| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. |
139	
140	Grade it with [`set_video`](/mcp/tools-set-video/): `color`, `wheels`, `curves`, `look`, `qualifier`, and the point filters (sepia, noir, vignette and invert). Its `opacity` is the grade's strength. On a track cut by a [matte](/canvas/matte-tracks/) it grades only inside the matte, and on a matte track it does nothing.
141	
142	It's refused:
143	
144	- inside a nest, whether you pass `scope` or a nest is open
145	- in any transition or overlap. Fade it with `opacity` instead.
146	
147	Later, `set_video` gives an error for blur, sharpen, pixelate or a blend mode on it. The step is called "Add Adjustment Clip".
148	
149	## `add_background`
150	
151	Puts a backdrop on a new back-most track, starting at 0 and running the timeline's length, as [**Clip ▸ Add Background**](/canvas/backgrounds/) does. The clip is named "Background".
152	
153	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
154	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
155	| `color` | array of four numbers | No | The plate's colour, as `[r, g, b, a]`, each from 0 to 1. White when left out. |
156	| `media` | integer | No | A media id to show instead of a colour. `import_media` adds a file. |
157	| `duration` | integer | No | Its length, in ticks. Default: the whole timeline's length, and never less than one frame. |
158	| `scope` | integer | No | The nest to add it in. |
159	| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. |
160	
161	With no arguments it's a canvas-sized white rectangle, which is what the menu's **Solid Color** row sends. It's white because the canvas is already black, so a black plate would appear to do nothing. A full-canvas gradient is this clip with [`set_shape`](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/)'s `gradient` after it.
162	
163	With `media` the picture goes there at Fill scale, where `add_clip` would Fit it, because a plate that leaves the canvas showing down one side has failed. A video plate stops where its file does, whatever `duration` says. A picture runs the timeline.
164	
165	It answers both `new_tracks` and `new_clips`, and the track holds the lower id.
166	
167	These are errors, and nothing is added:
168	
169	- `media` and `color` together
170	- a `duration` under one frame
171	- a media with no pictures, such as a sound file
172	- a colour that isn't four numbers from 0 to 1
173	
174	The step is called "Add Background".
175	
176	## `add_blurred_background`
177	
178	The screencast backdrop, as [**Clip ▸ Add Blurred Background**](/canvas/backgrounds/#blurred-background) does. It copies a clip onto a new back-most track at the same start, duration, speed and source window, so the two play exactly the same frames.
179	
180	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
181	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
182	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip id. `get_project` lists them. |
183	| `scope` | integer | No | The nest the clip is in. |
184	| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. |
185	
186	The copy is named "Blurred Background". It's scaled to fill the canvas, centred, uncropped, blended normally and blurred at full strength.
187	
188	Its sound is off, or the mix would play one recording twice. It drops the original's ducking, because a copy keeping it would duck the whole mix, and it drops its transition, actions and label too.
189	
190	It answers both `new_tracks` and `new_clips`, and the track holds the lower id.
191	
192	These are errors, and nothing is added:
193	
194	- a nest clip, whose copy would come out sharp
195	- a source with no pixel size, such as a text clip or a sound-only clip
196	- a clip with no video properties
197	
198	The step is called "Add Blurred Background".
199

1	---
2	title: "Tools: moving and trimming"
3	description: The agent tools that move clips, trim their edges, slip their source, roll a cut and switch a clip's picture or sound, with every argument and refusal.
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	These tools change where a clip sits and what it shows. They name clips by id, so read them from `get_project` first.
9	
10	<AtAGlance tools={['move_clip', 'trim_start', 'trim_end', 'slip', 'roll', 'set_enabled']} />
11	
12	## What the tools share
13	
14	Each one is one undo step. It answers `ok: true` and the `project` summary. See [What a call answers](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/).
15	
16	**Clamped, not refused.** Most of these hold a time to what the clip's source allows and do as much as they can. Read the clip back to see where it landed. When the limits leave nothing to do, the answer says "*Step* made no change", and no undo step is made.
17	
18	**Times** are ticks, 600,000 per second, rounded to the project's frame grid. See [Units and ids](/mcp/units-and-ids/).
19	
20	**`project`** is the path of an open project as `get_project` reports it. Without it the call goes to the frontmost project.
21	
22	**`scope`** is a nest id. With it, the call's ids and times are looked up inside that nest. Without it, the call goes wherever the app is looking. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/).
23	
24	**Linked pairs.** After [`detach_audio`](/mcp/tools-copy-and-nest/), a picture and its sound move together. The partner comes along only when it's on an unlocked track. A lock on a named clip's own track doesn't stop these tools.
25	
26	**A boolean** may also be sent as `"true"`, `"1"`, `"false"` or `"0"`.
27	
28	## `move_clip`
29	
30	Shifts clips along the timeline, and optionally onto another track, as [dragging a clip](/editing/move-clips/) does.
31	
32	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
33	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
34	| `clips` | array of integers | Yes | The clip ids. At least one. |
35	| `delta` | integer | Yes | How far to shift, in ticks. Negative moves earlier. |
36	| `track` | integer | No | The destination track for the first clip. The first clip is the one on the back-most track, then the earliest. Leave it out to stay on the current tracks. |
37	| `scope` | integer | No | The nest the clips are in. |
38	| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. |
39	
40	Several clips keep their relative track offsets, so a selection spanning two tracks lands two tracks apart.
41	
42	Starts stop at 0. It's the earliest clip that stops there, linked partners included, and the rest keep their distance from it.
43	
44	A linked pair moves together in time, but only the clips you name change track. So you can drop a sound half onto a track of its own while its picture stays.
45	
46	It's refused:
47	
48	- when the destination breaks the overlap rule: a clip may overlap at most one neighbour on each side, and each overlap may be at most half of the shorter clip
49	- when a clip would land off either end of the track list
50	
51	A clip that gains an overlap with the clip before it, and has no transition, gains a `cross_dissolve`. The step is called "Move Clip".
52	
53	## `trim_start`
54	
55	Moves a clip's start, as [dragging its left edge](/editing/trimming/) or pressing <kbd>W</kbd> does. The content stays in place: the source's in point advances by the same amount, so nothing after the new start shifts.
56	
57	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
58	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
59	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip id. |
60	| `to` | integer | Yes | The new start, in ticks. |
61	| `alone` | boolean | No | `true` moves this clip's edge without its linked partner's, which makes a [J-cut or L-cut](/audio/j-and-l-cuts/). The timeline does this for a dragged sound. Default `false`. |
62	| `scope` | integer | No | The nest the clip is in. |
63	| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. |
64	
65	It stops at the source's own beginning and one frame short of the clip's end, because a clip is at least one frame long.
66	
67	On a linked pair, the other half's start follows when it was the same as this clip's.
68	
69	Timed words stay on the speech they time, and a graphic's own clock moves with the edge. Actions stay where they are in the clip. See [What a trim keeps](/editing/trimming/#what-a-trim-keeps).
70	
71	On a clip with a [speed ramp](/speed/edit-a-ramped-clip/), the ramp stays where it is in the clip, so what plays after the new start can change. The start is held where the clip still fits its media.
72	
73	It's refused when the new start would break the overlap rule. The step is called "Trim Start".
74	
75	## `trim_end`
76	
77	Moves a clip's end, as [dragging its right edge](/editing/trimming/) or pressing <kbd>E</kbd> does.
78	
79	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
80	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
81	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip id. |
82	| `to` | integer | Yes | The new end, in ticks. |
83	| `alone` | boolean | No | `true` moves this clip's edge without its linked partner's, which makes a [J-cut or L-cut](/audio/j-and-l-cuts/). Default `false`. |
84	| `scope` | integer | No | The nest the clip is in. |
85	| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. |
86	
87	It stops at the last frame the source has left after the in point, and one frame after the clip's start.
88	
89	On a linked pair, the other half's end follows when it was the same as this clip's.
90	
91	It's refused when the new end would break the overlap rule. The step is called "Trim End".
92	
93	## `slip`
94	
95	Slides the source under a fixed clip, as [<kbd>⌥⇧</kbd>-dragging a clip's body](/editing/slip-and-roll/#slip-a-clip) does. What the clip shows changes, and where it sits doesn't, so nothing downstream moves.
96	
97	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
98	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
99	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip id. |
100	| `delta` | integer | Yes | How far to slide the source, in timeline ticks. The source moves by `delta` times the clip's speed. Positive shows later material. |
101	| `scope` | integer | No | The nest the clip is in. |
102	| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. |
103	
104	The slide stops so the window stays inside the media. A [freeze clip](/speed/freeze-frame/) moves the frame it holds instead, and stops one frame short of the file's end.
105	
106	A linked partner on an unlocked track slips too, by whichever of the two can move less, so the sound stays on its picture. Actions don't move.
107	
108	Any clip other than a media or freeze clip is an error. The step is called "Slip".
109	
110	## `roll`
111	
112	Moves a hard cut between two clips, as [<kbd>⌥⇧</kbd>-dragging a clip's edge](/editing/slip-and-roll/#roll-a-cut) does. This clip's start and the end of the clip before it both become `to`. One grows by exactly what the other loses, and the pair's outer edges and total length don't move.
113	
114	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
115	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
116	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip to the right of the cut. |
117	| `to` | integer | Yes | Where the cut moves to, in ticks. |
118	| `alone` | boolean | No | `true` moves this cut without rolling the linked partner's. Default `false`. |
119	| `scope` | integer | No | The nest the clip is in. |
120	| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. |
121	
122	The clip before is the one on the same track that ends exactly at this clip's start.
123	
124	The cut stops so each clip keeps a frame and neither asks for source it doesn't have. On a [speed ramp](/speed/edit-a-ramped-clip/) it's held where the clip still fits its media.
125	
126	The linked half of a pair rolls its own cut too, when it starts at the same time and has a hard cut of its own there.
127	
128	It's refused when no clip on the track ends where this one begins, with "no clip on track … ends where clip … begins". That covers a gap and an overlap. An overlap is a transition, so use [`set_transition_duration`](/mcp/tools-transitions/) to change its length. The step is called "Roll".
129	
130	## `set_enabled`
131	
132	Turns one clip's picture or sound on or off, the two halves [**Clip ▸ Detach Audio**](/editing/enable-picture-and-sound/) flips. A half that's off adds nothing to the picture or the mix, and the clip stays where it is.
133	
134	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
135	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
136	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip id. |
137	| `video` | boolean | No | Show this clip's picture. Left out, it stays as it is. |
138	| `audio` | boolean | No | Play this clip's sound. Left out, it stays as it is. |
139	| `scope` | integer | No | The nest the clip is in. |
140	| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. |
141	
142	It's refused when neither `video` nor `audio` is given. A value the clip already has changes nothing. The step is called "Clip Enabled".

3	/// `new_project_from_range` (spec §11 CJ-52; road map "creator-jobs" CJ5b),
4	/// mirroring File ▸ New Project from Range…
5	/// (`EditorViewController+NewFromRange.swift`): the top-level timeline's
6	/// `[from, to)` opened as a new project through `ProjectDocument.derived(…)`,
7	/// with the kept media's caches and the drawn graphics carried. Saved at
8	/// `path` when given, as `new_project` saves; untitled and dirty otherwise.
9	/// The source document never changes, so it makes no undo step there.
10	extension AgentServer {
11	
12	    /// Runs on the server thread (`creatorOffMainTools`), its body one main
13	    /// hop: the target, the nest refusal, the times, the path's refusals,
14	    /// then the door.
15	    func newProjectFromRange(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> String {
16	        guard !Thread.isMainThread else {
17	            throw ToolError(
18	                message: "new_project_from_range must run on the server thread — its name is "
19	                    + "missing from AgentServer.creatorOffMainTools.")
20	        }
21	        let path = try stringArg(a, "path")
22	        let display = Self.derivedDisplay
23	        return try onMain {
24	            let document = try target(a)
25	            guard document.scope == nil else {
26	                throw ToolError(
27	                    message: "new_project_from_range works on the top-level timeline: set_scope "
28	                        + "with no nest first.")
29	            }
30	            let from = try timeArg(a, "from", document)
31	            let to = try timeArg(a, "to", document)
32	            let url = path.map {
33	                Self.destinationURL($0, extension: ProjectDocument.projectFileExtension)
34	            }
35	            if let url {
36	                try refuseHeldPath(url, except: nil, tool: "new_project_from_range")
37	                guard !FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: url.path) else {
38	                    throw ToolError(
39	                        message: "\(url.path) already exists, so new_project_from_range did not "
40	                            + "write there: pass a new path.")
41	                }
42	            }
43	            let made: (document: ProjectDocument, carried: DerivedCarry.Report)
44	            do {
45	                made = try ProjectDocument.derived(
46	                    from: document, handle: document.project, range: (from: from, to: to),
47	                    path: url, display: display, name: "\(document.displayStem) (range)")
48	            } catch {
49	                throw ToolError(message: error.localizedDescription)
50	            }
51	            var result: [String: Any] = [
52	                "project": summary(made.document),
53	                "carried": [
54	                    "files": made.carried.files, "bytes": made.carried.bytes,
55	                    "seconds": made.carried.seconds,
56	                ],
57	            ]
58	            if let url { result["saved"] = url.path }
59	            return try jsonResult(result)
60	        }
61	    }
62	
63	    #if FRAMEJOB_DEV_TOOLS
64	    /// The dev-only launch default that opens the derived document with no
65	    /// window (`display: false`), so a proof can see the windowless door.
66	    static let derivedHiddenKey = "RCDevDerivedHidden"
67	    #endif
68	
69	    /// True but under `-RCDevDerivedHidden YES` in a build with the dev tools.
70	    static var derivedDisplay: Bool {
71	        #if FRAMEJOB_DEV_TOOLS
72	        return !UserDefaults.standard.bool(forKey: derivedHiddenKey)
73	        #else
74	        return true
75	        #endif
76	    }
77	}

3	/// The agent's mirrors of Edit ▸ Undo (⌘Z) and Edit ▸ Redo (⇧⌘Z).
4	///
5	/// Every other agent tool is an edit, and `ProjectDocument.performGroupedEdit`
6	/// already turns each one into exactly one undo step (app/CLAUDE.md). Without
7	/// these two the agent could make those steps and never walk them, so the one
8	/// property the whole undo design rests on — one edit is one step, and undoing
9	/// it restores the frame — could not be checked by driving the built app,
10	/// which spec §10 step 7 asks for.
11	extension AgentServer {
12	
13	    /// `undo` — Edit ▸ Undo. One step, and the step's action name comes back
14	    /// so a caller can see what it walked past.
15	    func undoEdit(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> String {
16	        try walkHistory(a, redo: false)
17	    }
18	
19	    /// `redo` — Edit ▸ Redo.
20	    func redoEdit(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> String {
21	        try walkHistory(a, redo: true)
22	    }
23	
24	    /// **Pitfall** (app/CLAUDE.md, and the same one `performGroupedEdit`
25	    /// documents): a tool call is not an AppKit event, so with `groupsByEvent`
26	    /// on, `NSUndoManager` opens an implicit per-event group that nothing ever
27	    /// closes. `undo()` closes the top-level group before undoing, which
28	    /// against that phantom group leaves an end with no begin and hangs the
29	    /// next save inside its file coordinator. Turning event grouping off for
30	    /// the duration — never "flushing" the level — is the same discipline
31	    /// every off-event path here follows.
32	    private func walkHistory(_ a: [String: Any], redo: Bool) throws -> String {
33	        let document = try target(a)
34	        guard let manager = document.undoManager else {
35	            throw ToolError(message: "This project has no undo history.")
36	        }
37	        guard redo ? manager.canRedo : manager.canUndo else {
38	            throw ToolError(
39	                message: redo
40	                    ? "There is nothing to redo. Only an undo makes a redo step."
41	                    : "There is nothing to undo. Only an edit makes an undo step; "
42	                        + "set_playhead and set_range are view state and make none.")
43	        }
44	        let name = (redo ? manager.redoActionName : manager.undoActionName)
45	        let groupsByEvent = manager.groupsByEvent
46	        if groupsByEvent { manager.groupsByEvent = false }
47	        if redo { manager.redo() } else { manager.undo() }
48	        if groupsByEvent { manager.groupsByEvent = true }
49	        return try jsonResult([
50	            "ok": true,
51	            redo ? "redone" : "undone": name.isEmpty ? "Edit" : name,
52	            "can_undo": manager.canUndo,
53	            "can_redo": manager.canRedo,
54	            "project": summary(document),
55	        ])
56	    }
57	}

3	/// Editing INSIDE a nest over MCP, and looking inside one: the envelope's
4	/// `scope` (spec §6, `core/src/scope.rs`) and the `set_scope` tool that
5	/// mirrors the double-click (road map 2's phase 9).
6	///
7	/// **The whole surface is arguments on tools that already existed.** No op
8	/// was added — `rc_op_names` was unchanged — so the catalog grew one property,
9	/// injected once in `AgentCatalog.tool` for every name the core calls an op,
10	/// and one tool, which is not an op either. What that buys is the thing the
11	/// spec designed and left (§4.4): every row of §6 can now name a clip, a
12	/// track or an action inside a nest.
13	///
14	/// Three pieces, and the split between them is the point:
15	///
16	///  - **The scope is read ONCE, at the dispatch.** `AgentServer.dispatch` is
17	///    the only place holding both a tool's name and its arguments for all
18	///    seventy-five of them, so it reads `scope` there and leaves it on
19	///    `callScope` for the length of the call; `performGroupedEdit` stamps it
20	///    onto every op through `addressed` below. Fifty-eight handlers were not
21	///    touched and cannot forget.
22	///  - **The id readers resolve against a CONTAINER.** `idScope` below is what
23	///    `clipArg`, `clipsArg`, `optionalClipsArg` and `trackArg` ask, so
24	///    `trim_start {clip: <inside the nest>, scope: 4}` finds its clip instead
25	///    of being refused by the app before the core ever saw the scope. That
26	///    was the real work of this phase on this side, and the road map does not
27	///    mention it.
28	///  - **`set_scope` is view state and edits nothing**, exactly like
29	///    `set_playhead`, `set_range` and `set_selection`. It exists because
30	///    `get_project` and `render_frame` answer about what the app is LOOKING
31	///    at, and without it there was no way to make them look inside. An op
32	///    sent while it is open follows it unless it carries a `scope` of its
33	///    own — `effectiveScope` below is that rule and argues it.
34	///
35	/// **Two composites take no scope ARGUMENT and still work inside a nest**,
36	/// and the ops-only injection rule excludes them without an exception list:
37	/// `detect_silence` and `normalize_clip` are not §6 rows. They follow the
38	/// VIEW instead, from both ends at once — their ids resolve through
39	/// `idScope` like every other tool's, and `SilenceDetector.read` /
40	/// `AudioNormalize.read` compute from `ProjectDocument.editedProject`'s plan,
41	/// which is the same container — so the pair is coherent rather than half
42	/// converted. What they cannot do is be pointed at a nest nobody is looking
43	/// at, and that is the argument for leaving it there: each one measures a
44	/// PLAN, the app memoises exactly one scoped handle (the open one), and a
45	/// per-call `scope` would mean building a second project per call and
46	/// mapping every tick in the answer back out of it. Nothing is lost that a
47	/// caller cannot reach — `set_scope`, then ask — and `ripple_delete_ranges`,
48	/// which is what `detect_silence`'s answer is fed to, takes a scope like any
49	/// other op.
50	///
51	/// There is also a spelling hazard here worth naming, since it is the reason
52	/// to think twice before changing that: `detect_silence` already answers a
53	/// RESULT key called `scope`, meaning which set of CLIPS it measured.
54	/// Nothing keeps those two words apart but the fact that one is an input and
55	/// the other an answer, so a `detect_silence` that ever took the envelope's
56	/// scope would have to say in both descriptions which is which.
57	///
58	/// **The captions group used to be the one place this did NOT line up, and
59	/// the way it was settled is the rule for the next producer.** Every one of
60	/// them — `CaptionImporter.plan(for:in:)`, `Transcriber`,
61	/// `TranscribeSheetController` and `CaptionExporter`, on the File-menu path
62	/// and the tool path alike — built its plan from `document.project`, the
63	/// DOCUMENT, while the ops that plan produced were addressed to whatever nest
64	/// was open, here and in `ProjectDocument.addressed(_:)` alike. So with a nest
65	/// open they measured a placement against the timeline and then placed it
66	/// inside the nest, and the menu item had exactly the same defect as the tool.
67	/// All four read `editedProject` now, as `SilenceDetector` and
68	/// `AudioNormalize` do. **A producer reads the container it writes into** —
69	/// that is the whole rule, it is cheaper than making the ops document-level,
70	/// and it is what a fifth producer should copy.
71	extension AgentServer {
72	
73	    // MARK: - The call's scope
74	
75	    /// Refuses a `scope` that names no nest in `document`, by name.
76	    ///
77	    /// Called from `target(_:)`, which every handler passes through before it
78	    /// reads a single argument, so the ORDER `core/src/scope.rs` documents
79	    /// holds on this side too: an unknown nest is answered FIRST, ahead of
80	    /// the op's own arguments, because it is the argument that decides which
81	    /// container the caller thinks it is editing.
82	    ///
83	    /// The sentence is the CORE's, word for word, with the app's own
84	    /// direction added after it. Both layers can answer this — the app for
85	    /// every op tool, the core for anything that reaches it another way — and
86	    /// a caller (or a proof) that learns one spelling should not have to
87	    /// learn a second.
88	    func checkCallScope(_ document: ProjectDocument) throws {
89	        guard let scope = callScope else { return }
90	        guard document.project.snapshot.nest(scope) != nil else {
91	            throw ToolError(
92	                message: "no nest with id \(scope). get_project lists them under nests, and a "
93	                    + "nest clip's source.project names the one it shows.")
94	        }
95	    }
96	
97	    /// The container this call's id arguments resolve in: the timeline, or
98	    /// the nest the envelope's `scope` named.
99	    ///
100	    /// It reads the PARENT snapshot rather than building a scoped handle,
101	    /// which is the cheap half of `core/src/scope.rs`'s view and the only
102	    /// half an id lookup needs: a nest holds its tracks and clips in the
103	    /// parent's one id space (spec §5.2), so `snapshot.nests[]` already has
104	    /// them. `NestScope` next door reads the path the same way and for the
105	    /// same reason.
106	    /// The nest a call is really acting in: its own `scope` when it has one,
107	    /// else the nest the APP has open (`set_scope`), else nil.
108	    ///
109	    /// **The argument overrides the view; an absent argument follows it.**
110	    /// That is the whole rule, and it is the one that makes every other piece
111	    /// agree with itself. `get_project` reports the open container, so the
112	    /// ids a caller reads back are that container's; `render_frame` draws it;
113	    /// `detect_silence`, `normalize_clip` and `sync_audio` compute from
114	    /// `ProjectDocument.editedProject`'s plan, which is that container's too;
115	    /// and `ProjectDocument.addressed(_:)` already stamps the open nest onto
116	    /// every op the APP sends, so an agent that inherits it is doing exactly
117	    /// what the person at the keyboard does. The alternative — the argument
118	    /// or nothing — was written first and thrown away: it made
119	    /// `get_project` list clips that the very next op could not name, and it
120	    /// would have left the three composites resolving their ids in one
121	    /// container and reading their plan from another.
122	    ///
123	    /// What it costs is the spelling of "edit the timeline while I am looking
124	    /// inside a nest", which is now `set_scope` with no arguments first. That
125	    /// is the same thing the UI costs a person, and it is worth less than the
126	    /// coherence.
127	    func effectiveScope(_ document: ProjectDocument) -> UInt32? {
128	        callScope ?? document.scope
129	    }
130	
131	    /// The container this call's id arguments resolve in — `effectiveScope`'s
132	    /// nest, or the timeline.
133	    ///
134	    /// It reads the PARENT snapshot rather than building a scoped handle,
135	    /// which is the cheap half of `core/src/scope.rs`'s view and the only
136	    /// half an id lookup needs: a nest holds its tracks and clips in the
137	    /// parent's one id space (spec §5.2), so `snapshot.nests[]` already has
138	    /// them. `NestScope` next door reads the path the same way and for the
139	    /// same reason.
140	    func idScope(_ document: ProjectDocument) throws -> AgentIdScope {
141	        let snapshot = document.project.snapshot
142	        guard let scope = effectiveScope(document) else {
143	            return AgentIdScope(
144	                nest: nil, clips: snapshot.clips, tracks: snapshot.tracks, fromArgument: false)
145	        }
146	        // Unreachable through `target(_:)`, which has already refused an
147	        // unknown `scope` argument, and through `clampViewState`, which
148	        // clears a view path whose nest has gone. It is here so the function
149	        // is total rather than optional-returning: a reader that fell back to
150	        // the timeline when the nest was missing would answer "No clip has id
151	        // 17" for a call whose real mistake was the scope.
152	        guard let nest = snapshot.nest(scope) else {
153	            try checkCallScope(document)
154	            return AgentIdScope(
155	                nest: nil, clips: snapshot.clips, tracks: snapshot.tracks, fromArgument: false)
156	        }
157	        return AgentIdScope(
158	            nest: nest, clips: nest.clips, tracks: nest.tracks, fromArgument: callScope != nil)
159	    }
160	
161	    /// The scope stamped onto the ops of one agent edit — `performGroupedEdit`
162	    /// in the frozen file calls this, and it is the MCP mirror of
163	    /// `ProjectDocument.addressed(_:)`.
164	    ///
165	    /// **Two rules, and the difference between them is deliberate.** An
166	    /// EXPLICIT `scope` is stamped on every op, the seven document-level ones
167	    /// included, so an agent that asks for `add_media {scope: 4}` gets the
168	    /// core's own refusal by name rather than a silent redirection — it asked
169	    /// a question and the answer is no (`ReelOp.documentLevelNames` argues
170	    /// the other half of this). An INHERITED one skips them, exactly as
171	    /// `addressed` does, because a Finder drop inside a nest is an
172	    /// `add_media` on the document's one media list plus an `add_clip` in the
173	    /// nest, and an agent's `import_media` inside a nest is the same act.
174	    ///
175	    /// **Two of those seven may not be sent that way at all**, and
176	    /// `checkDocumentLevelTicks` below is the refusal: `add_marker` and a
177	    /// `set_marker` carrying a `time` would reach the timeline's `markers[]`
178	    /// at a tick the caller measured from the NEST's zero. Read the two
179	    /// together — this method decides which container an op is addressed to,
180	    /// and that one decides which ops may take the unscoped answer.
181	    ///
182	    /// It mirrors that method rather than calling it because `addressed` is
183	    /// private to `ProjectDocument` — but the two must not drift, and the
184	    /// reason is not tidiness: `AgentServer.performGroupedEdit` TRIES the ops
185	    /// on the handle first, purely, to turn a refusal into a message instead
186	    /// of a beep, and a trial addressed differently from the commit would
187	    /// report a failure the commit would not have had.
188	    func addressed(_ ops: [ReelOp], _ document: ProjectDocument) -> [ReelOp] {
189	        if let scope = callScope { return ops.map { $0.scoped(scope) } }
190	        guard let view = document.scope else { return ops }
191	        return ops.map { $0.isDocumentLevel ? $0 : $0.scoped(view) }
192	    }
193	
194	    /// Refuses the ops an INHERITED scope would send at a tick measured from
195	    /// the wrong zero — `add_marker`, and `set_marker`'s `time`.
196	    ///
197	    /// **This is the tool path's copy of a decision the app made first.**
198	    /// `addressed` above sends the seven document-level ops UNSCOPED out of a
199	    /// scope it inherited, so `core/src/scope.rs`'s `refused_inside` never
200	    /// fires for them and they land on the document. For five of the seven
201	    /// that is exactly right, and it is why File ▸ Add Media…, a Relink, a
202	    /// Remove and the Document tab's canvas rows all go on working with a nest
203	    /// open. For the two that carry a TICK it is a wrong PLACEMENT reported as
204	    /// success: while a scope is open `ProjectDocument.playhead` is
205	    /// NEST-LOCAL, `get_project` answers the nest's clips and duration,
206	    /// `set_playhead` writes the nest's own time and `render_frame` draws the
207	    /// nest — so a caller working in the open container hands over a
208	    /// nest-local tick and the marker appears somewhere else on the timeline,
209	    /// with an `ok` on it. The app decided this already:
210	    /// `EditorViewController+NestScope.validateNestScopeAction` greys Add
211	    /// Marker out inside a nest and `addMarkerCommand` carries its own guard
212	    /// for the bare-M key, both for this exact reason. This is that refusal,
213	    /// worded for a caller who gets a sentence rather than a dead menu item.
214	    ///
215	    /// **`remove_marker` is deliberately NOT here, and neither is a
216	    /// `set_marker` that carries no `time`.** Both name an id and read no
217	    /// clock, so there is no zero for either to be measured from — and both
218	    /// are LIVE in the app with a nest open, in the Document tab's marker
219	    /// table, which is about the FILE and reads `documentSnapshot` for that
220	    /// very reason (app/CLAUDE.md). Refusing them would make these tools less
221	    /// of a mirror of the UI than they already are, and would charge a rename
222	    /// two `set_scope` calls and a re-entry for nothing. That the marker id is
223	    /// the DOCUMENT's is already settled and already said: `markerArg` resolves
224	    /// it against the timeline's markers on purpose, so that the core's own
225	    /// sentence rather than "No marker has id 12" is what a scoped call hears.
226	    ///
227	    /// An EXPLICIT `scope` is left alone. It is stamped on all seven and the
228	    /// core answers `"add_marker has no meaning inside nest N"` by name, which
229	    /// is the designed answer to a caller that asked the question outright
230	    /// (`addressed`'s two rules, and `ReelOp.documentLevelNames`).
231	    ///
232	    /// It is called from `AgentServer.performGroupedEdit` — the one place
233	    /// every editing tool passes through, the handlers that call it directly
234	    /// rather than through `editResult` included — so no handler has to
235	    /// remember it and a later composite that builds a marker op inherits it.
236	    /// What being there rather than at the two handlers' heads costs is the
237	    /// ORDER of one refusal: a call whose `at` is ALSO unreadable hears about
238	    /// the `at` first, because the handler reads its arguments before it
239	    /// reaches the edit. That is a true complaint either way, which is what
240	    /// makes it a fair price here and not in `checkCallScope`'s case — there
241	    /// the mistake being reported is which document the caller thinks it is
242	    /// editing, and it outranks everything.
243	    func checkDocumentLevelTicks(_ ops: [ReelOp], _ document: ProjectDocument) throws {
244	        guard callScope == nil, let view = document.scope else { return }
245	        for op in ops {
246	            switch op.name {
247	            case "add_marker":
248	                throw ToolError(
249	                    message: "add_marker has no meaning inside nest \(view): a nest has no "
250	                        + "markers, and every tick in this call is measured from that nest's "
251	                        + "own zero, so the marker would land somewhere else on the timeline. "
252	                        + "set_scope with no arguments comes back out; then add_marker at a "
253	                        + "project time. The app greys Add Marker out in here for the same "
254	                        + "reason.")
255	            case "set_marker" where op.args["time"] != nil:
256	                throw ToolError(
257	                    message: "set_marker's time has no meaning inside nest \(view): a marker's "
258	                        + "time is the timeline's, and every tick in this call is measured "
259	                        + "from that nest's own zero. set_scope with no arguments comes back "
260	                        + "out; then set_marker at a project time. Its name, chapter and color "
261	                        + "mean the same thing in either container and are accepted in here, "
262	                        + "which is what the Document tab's marker table does with a nest "
263	                        + "open.")
264	            default:
265	                continue
266	            }
267	        }
268	    }
269	
270	    /// Where an edit's ops actually LANDED, as the result reports it: the nest
271	    /// whose id was stamped on them, and the names of any that went to the
272	    /// document instead.
273	    ///
274	    /// **It is read off what `addressed` STAMPS and never off
275	    /// `effectiveScope`**, and that difference is the whole reason it exists.
276	    /// `editResult` used to echo the effective scope unconditionally, which is
277	    /// a statement about the VIEW; `addressed` sends the seven document-level
278	    /// ops unscoped out of an inherited one, which is a statement about the
279	    /// EDIT. So a `remove_media`, a `set_canvas` or a marker rename sent with
280	    /// a nest open reported that it had landed inside that nest when it had
281	    /// landed on the document — a tool misreporting WHERE an edit went, which
282	    /// is the class of defect this phase already fixed once at the merge seam
283	    /// (`performGroupedEdit`'s closing guard).
284	    ///
285	    /// **The MIXED edit is why `document_ops` is a list and not a flag.** One
286	    /// edit can legitimately span both containers — a Finder drop inside a
287	    /// nest is `add_media` on the document plus `add_clip` in the nest, as ONE
288	    /// undo step (`ReelOp.documentLevelNames` argues it) — and there is no
289	    /// single number that describes that, which is exactly the mistake being
290	    /// fixed. So both halves are named: `scope` is the nest the scoped ops
291	    /// carried and `document_ops` is every op that skipped it, and a result
292	    /// carrying both says which of its ops went where. No tool sends such a
293	    /// mix TODAY — an agent's `import_media` and `add_clip` are two calls, and
294	    /// `add_background`'s Image… composite is the menu's rather than the
295	    /// tool's — but the account has to be right before the composite that does
296	    /// arrives, and nobody reading one of these results should have to know
297	    /// which handlers mix and which do not.
298	    ///
299	    /// With no scope anywhere it answers nothing at all, so every ordinary
300	    /// result is byte for byte the one it always was.
301	    func scopeLanding(_ ops: [ReelOp], _ document: ProjectDocument) -> [String: Any] {
302	        guard effectiveScope(document) != nil else { return [:] }
303	        let stamped = addressed(ops, document)
304	        var result: [String: Any] = [:]
305	        // Uniform by construction: `addressed` stamps ONE scope on every op it
306	        // stamps at all, so the first one found is the answer for all of them.
307	        if let nest = stamped.compactMap({ $0.scope }).first { result["scope"] = Int(nest) }
308	        let onDocument = stamped.filter { $0.scope == nil }.map { $0.name }
309	        if !onDocument.isEmpty { result["document_ops"] = onDocument }
310	        return result
311	    }

314	
315	    /// Part 4 of `AgentServer.catalogParityFailure`: every OP tool declares
316	    /// the envelope's `scope`.
317	    ///
318	    /// **It is here because parts 1 to 3 cannot see an OMISSION.** They
319	    /// compare name SETS and read each schema's shape, so a tool that quietly
320	    /// lacks an argument passes all three — and a scope-less op tool is
321	    /// exactly that: the server starts clean, the op works on the timeline,
322	    /// and editing inside a nest is unreachable through it with nothing
323	    /// anywhere saying so. `AgentCatalog.tool`'s injection makes that hard to
324	    /// do by hand, but the fifty-sixth op arriving with a hand-written schema,
325	    /// or an `opNames` that came back short, both land here.
326	    ///
327	    /// It reads the CATALOG rather than asking whether the injection ran,
328	    /// which is the only way it can catch anything: a check that asked
329	    /// `AgentCatalog.tool` about itself would be testing the check. Members
330	    /// of `opsWithoutTools` are skipped for part 2's reason — there is no
331	    /// tool to declare anything. It costs nothing to run: the tools array is
332	    /// already parsed and the op list already read.
333	    static func scopeFailure(_ tools: [[String: Any]], _ ops: Set<String>) -> String? {
334	        let scopeless =
335	            tools
336	            .filter { tool in
337	                guard let name = tool["name"] as? String, ops.contains(name) else { return false }
338	                let properties = (tool["inputSchema"] as? [String: Any])?["properties"]
339	                    as? [String: Any]
340	                return properties?["scope"] == nil
341	            }
342	            .compactMap { $0["name"] as? String }.sorted()
343	        guard scopeless.isEmpty else {
344	            return "these op tools do not declare scope: \(scopeless) — every row of spec §6 "
345	                + "can be sent inside a nest (core/src/scope.rs), and a tool that does not "
346	                + "say so is one an agent cannot use in there"
347	        }
348	        return nil
349	    }

351	    // MARK: - set_scope
352	
353	    /// `set_scope` — double-clicking a nest clip, Clip ▸ Open Nest (⌘↓) and
354	    /// Clip ▸ Close Nest (⌘↑) (`EditorViewController+NestScope.swift`).
355	    ///
356	    /// View state like the playhead, the range and the selection: no op runs,
357	    /// nothing is undoable and the project is untouched. What it moves is
358	    /// what `get_project` reports and `render_frame` draws, which is the only
359	    /// way an agent can SEE what an edit inside a nest did.
360	    ///
361	    /// **It is ABSOLUTE**, like the other three `set_` tools: the argument
362	    /// names where to BE, not a step to take, so `set_scope {clip: 41}` means
363	    /// the same thing from the timeline and from three levels down. That is
364	    /// what makes it usable without first reading the current scope back —
365	    /// and it is why `clip` accepts a nest clip in ANY container, since the
366	    /// path down to a given id is determined (one id space, and a nest cannot
367	    /// show itself at any remove).
368	    func setScope(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> String {
369	        let document = try target(a)
370	        let path = try nestScopePath(a, document)
371	        applyNestScope(path, document)
372	        var result: [String: Any] = ["ok": true]
373	        result.merge(scopeReport(document)) { _, new in new }
374	        result["playhead"] = document.playhead
375	        result["project"] = summary(document)
376	        return try jsonResult(result)
377	    }
378	
379	    /// `set_scope`'s two arguments read into the path they name.
380	    ///
381	    /// `nest` and `clip` are two spellings of one destination and at most one
382	    /// may be given; neither means the timeline. They are not interchangeable
383	    /// and the tool says so: `clip` names the nest AND the start the times
384	    /// inside are measured from, which is what a double-click has and what
385	    /// two clips showing one nest do not share, while `nest` is the number an
386	    /// op's own `scope` takes and is the one an agent already has in its
387	    /// hand.
388	    private func nestScopePath(_ a: [String: Any], _ document: ProjectDocument) throws
389	        -> [NestScopeStep]
390	    {
391	        let snapshot = document.project.snapshot
392	        let wantsNest = a["nest"] != nil && !(a["nest"] is NSNull)
393	        let wantsClip = a["clip"] != nil && !(a["clip"] is NSNull)
394	        guard !(wantsNest && wantsClip) else {
395	            throw ToolError(
396	                message: "Pass nest or clip, not both — they are two spellings of one "
397	                    + "destination, and clip is the precise one.")
398	        }
399	        if wantsClip {
400	            let id = try idArg(a, "clip")
401	            guard let path = Self.pathToClip(id, in: snapshot) else {
402	                throw ToolError(
403	                    message: "No clip has id \(id), in this timeline or in any of its nests. "
404	                        + "get_project lists the clips, and each nest's own under nests.")
405	            }
406	            guard let clip = NestScope.clips(in: path, of: snapshot)
407	                .first(where: { $0.id == id }), let nest = clip.source.nestID
408	            else {
409	                throw ToolError(
410	                    message: "Clip \(id) does not show a nest, so there is nothing to open "
411	                        + "inside it. A nest clip's source.kind is \"nest\".")
412	            }
413	            return path + [NestScopeStep(nest: nest, clip: id)]
414	        }
415	        if wantsNest {
416	            let id = try idArg(a, "nest")
417	            guard snapshot.nest(id) != nil else {
418	                throw ToolError(
419	                    message: "no nest with id \(id). get_project lists them under nests.")
420	            }
421	            // The earliest TIMELINE clip that shows it, ties to the lower id.
422	            // A nest shown only from INSIDE another nest is refused rather
423	            // than guessed at: this is the view, and the app's way in is a
424	            // clip you can point at. `clip` reaches it, and so does an op's
425	            // own scope, which needs no view at all.
426	            guard let entry = snapshot.clips
427	                .filter({ $0.source.nestID == id })
428	                .min(by: { ($0.start, $0.id) < ($1.start, $1.id) })
429	            else {
430	                throw ToolError(
431	                    message: "No clip on the timeline shows nest \(id), so the view cannot "
432	                        + "reach it in one step. Name the nest CLIP instead — set_scope "
433	                        + "{clip: <id>} works at any depth — or send the op itself with "
434	                        + "scope: \(id), which needs no view.")
435	            }
436	            return [NestScopeStep(nest: id, clip: entry.id)]
437	        }
438	        return []
439	    }
440	
441	    /// The path from the timeline down to whichever container holds `clip`,
442	    /// or nil when no container does.
443	    ///
444	    /// A breadth-first walk over the containers, with the nests it has
445	    /// entered remembered: `check_nesting` refuses a cycle, so the visited
446	    /// set is belt and braces against a hand-written file rather than against
447	    /// anything the ops can make — but a walk that can be handed a project
448	    /// from disk does not get to assume the file is sane.
449	    private static func pathToClip(_ clip: UInt32, in snapshot: ProjectSnapshot)
450	        -> [NestScopeStep]?
451	    {
452	        var queue: [[NestScopeStep]] = [[]]
453	        var seen: Set<UInt32> = []
454	        while !queue.isEmpty {
455	            let path = queue.removeFirst()
456	            let clips = NestScope.clips(in: path, of: snapshot)
457	            if clips.contains(where: { $0.id == clip }) { return path }
458	            for candidate in clips {
459	                guard let nest = candidate.source.nestID, seen.insert(nest).inserted else {
460	                    continue
461	                }
462	                queue.append(path + [NestScopeStep(nest: nest, clip: candidate.id)])
463	            }
464	        }
465	        return nil
466	    }
467	
468	    /// Moves the document to `path`, through the editor's own gestures where
469	    /// there is an editor.
470	    ///
471	    /// **The gestures are reused rather than re-derived**, which matters
472	    /// because entering maps the playhead (`t − nest_clip.start`) and leaving
473	    /// maps it back and re-selects the clip: leave to the common prefix, then
474	    /// enter one step at a time, and an agent's scope change is the same
475	    /// event as a person's double-click — the player seeked, the timeline
476	    /// scrolled, the breadcrumb redrawn.
477	    ///
478	    /// A windowless document (which an agent can make) has no gestures, so it
479	    /// gets `setNestPath` directly with the playhead mapped through
480	    /// `NestScope.offset` — the same sum `enterNest` arrives at one clip
481	    /// start at a time, which is why the two cannot disagree.
482	    private func applyNestScope(_ path: [NestScopeStep], _ document: ProjectDocument) {
483	        guard path != document.nestPath else { return }
484	        let snapshot = document.project.snapshot
485	        guard let editor = editor(document) else {
486	            let project = document.playhead + NestScope.offset(of: document.nestPath, in: snapshot)
487	            let inside = max(0, project - NestScope.offset(of: path, in: snapshot))
488	            // Coming OUT re-selects the nest clip that was entered, the way
489	            // `leaveNest` does; going in selects nothing, the way `enterNest`
490	            // does. "Coming out" is the case where the new path is a proper
491	            // prefix of the old one.
492	            let shared = Self.commonPrefix(document.nestPath, path)
493	            let selection: Set<UInt32> =
494	                path.count == shared && document.nestPath.count > shared
495	                ? [document.nestPath[shared].clip] : []
496	            document.setNestPath(path, playhead: inside, selection: selection)
497	            return
498	        }
499	        editor.leaveAllNests(to: Self.commonPrefix(document.nestPath, path))
500	        for step in path.dropFirst(document.nestPath.count) {
501	            guard let clip = NestScope.clips(in: document.nestPath, of: snapshot)
502	                .first(where: { $0.id == step.clip })
503	            else { break }
504	            editor.enterNest(clip)
505	        }
506	    }
507	
508	    /// How many leading steps two paths share.
509	    private static func commonPrefix(_ a: [NestScopeStep], _ b: [NestScopeStep]) -> Int {
510	        var shared = 0
511	        while shared < a.count, shared < b.count, a[shared] == b[shared] { shared += 1 }
512	        return shared
513	    }
514	
515	    /// The scope as `get_project` and `set_scope` both report it.
516	    ///
517	    /// `scope` is the NEST id and nothing else, because it is the number an
518	    /// op's own `scope` argument takes: a caller copies it straight across.
519	    /// The clip it was entered through and the whole trail ride beside it
520	    /// under their own names, and the whole group is `{"scope": null}` at the
521	    /// timeline rather than absent, so "not in a nest" is an answer rather
522	    /// than a missing key.
523	    func scopeReport(_ document: ProjectDocument) -> [String: Any] {
524	        guard let step = document.nestPath.last else { return ["scope": NSNull()] }
525	        let snapshot = document.project.snapshot
526	        let names = NestScope.names(of: document.nestPath, in: snapshot)
527	        let trail = document.nestPath.enumerated().map { index, step -> [String: Any] in
528	            // `names` opens with "Timeline", so a step's own name is one
529	            // further along than its index.
530	            ["nest": Int(step.nest), "clip": Int(step.clip), "name": names[index + 1]]
531	        }
532	        return [
533	            "scope": Int(step.nest),
534	            "scope_clip": Int(step.clip),
535	            "scope_path": trail,
536	        ]
537	    }
538	}
539	
540	/// The container a call's id arguments are looked up in — the timeline, or
541	/// the nest the envelope's `scope` named.
542	///
543	/// It is a value rather than a `ProjectSnapshot` of the view because an id
544	/// lookup wants two lists and nothing else: assembling a whole view snapshot
545	/// per reader would mean a second Swift spelling of `scoped_view`'s table
546	/// (the canvas, the media, the emptied nest row) whose only reader compares
547	/// integers. `core/src/scope.rs` owns that table, and it owns it alone.
548	struct AgentIdScope {
549	    /// nil on the timeline.
550	    let nest: NestSnapshot?
551	    let clips: [ClipSnapshot]
552	    let tracks: [TrackSnapshot]
553	    /// Whether the nest came from the call's own `scope` or from the nest the
554	    /// app has open. It changes nothing about the lookup and one thing about
555	    /// the message: how to get back to the timeline is a different sentence
556	    /// for each.
557	    let fromArgument: Bool
558	
559	    func clip(_ id: UInt32) -> ClipSnapshot? { clips.first { $0.id == id } }
560	    func track(_ id: UInt32) -> TrackSnapshot? { tracks.first { $0.id == id } }
561	
562	    /// One track's clips in timeline order — `ProjectSnapshot.clips(onTrack:)`
563	    /// asked of this container instead of the document, which is what
564	    /// `remove_track`'s "still holds N clips" has to count inside a nest.
565	    func clips(onTrack id: UInt32) -> [ClipSnapshot] {
566	        clips.filter { $0.track == id }.sorted { $0.start < $1.start }
567	    }
568	
569	    /// "No clip has id 17. get_project lists the clips." — and inside a
570	    /// scope, the same sentence saying WHERE it looked.
571	    ///
572	    /// The unscoped spelling is byte for byte the one every one of these
573	    /// readers has answered since M2, deliberately: it is what the tools'
574	    /// own descriptions promise and what several proof scripts match on.
575	    ///
576	    /// The scoped one ends by saying how to get OUT, which is a different
577	    /// sentence depending on how the call got in — dropping an argument does
578	    /// nothing about a nest the window has open, and closing the nest does
579	    /// nothing about an argument.
580	    func noSuchId(_ kind: String, _ id: UInt32) -> String {
581	        guard let nest = nest else {
582	            return "No \(kind) has id \(id). get_project lists the \(kind)s."
583	        }
584	        let out =
585	            fromArgument
586	            ? "drop the scope to name one on the timeline"
587	            : "that nest is OPEN in the view, so ids mean its own — set_scope with no "
588	                + "arguments comes back out"
589	        return "No \(kind) has id \(id) inside nest \(nest.id). get_project lists that nest's "
590	            + "\(kind)s under nests; \(out)."
591	    }
592	}
