74	    /// The longest one import's own runs can take (spec §11 #227; the time it
75	    /// queues behind another import's conversion is not counted): the opt-in
76	    /// ffmpeg step's own bound, both attempts (`FFmpegRewrap.longestAssist`:
77	    /// the plan, the frame check, the encoder query, a VP9 copy and then its
78	    /// re-encode, and `run`'s grace on each of those five runs), plus three
79	    /// header probes (`MediaImporter.probeTimeout`: the source, the copy and
80	    /// the re-encode). `import_media` and `relink_media` both wait this long.
81	    static let probeCeiling: TimeInterval =
82	        FFmpegRewrap.longestAssist + 3 * MediaImporter.probeTimeout
83	
84	    /// Probes one file and waits for the answer. MUST run off the main thread
85	    /// — see `importMedia` — and gives up only after `probeCeiling`: a file
86	    /// AVFoundation cannot read may be converted by ffmpeg first
87	    /// (`FFmpegRewrap.assist`), which legitimately takes as long as
88	    /// `FFmpegRewrap.longestAssist`, so a shorter wait would answer a
89	    /// timeout while the conversion is still running. A tool call never
90	    /// asks the conversion question (spec §11 MC-5), so it passes
91	    /// `mayAsk: false`, and a refusal ffmpeg could have helped names the
92	    /// setting (`neverAsksSentence`).
93	    private func probe(_ url: URL) throws -> MediaDescriptor {
94	        guard !Thread.isMainThread else {
95	            throw ToolError(message: "Probing cannot run on the main thread.")
96	        }
97	        let semaphore = DispatchSemaphore(value: 0)
98	        let box = AgentBox<Result<MediaDescriptor, any Error>>()
99	        MediaImporter.probe(url: url, mayAsk: false) { result in
100	            box.value = result
101	            semaphore.signal()
102	        }
103	        guard semaphore.wait(timeout: .now() + Self.probeCeiling) == .success else {
104	            throw ToolError(message: "Timed out reading \(url.lastPathComponent).")
105	        }
106	        guard let outcome = box.value else {
107	            throw ToolError(message: "Could not read \(url.lastPathComponent).")
108	        }
109	        do {
110	            return try outcome.get()
111	        } catch {
112	            guard let sentence = Self.neverAsksSentence(for: error, url: url) else {
113	                throw ToolError(message: error.localizedDescription)
114	            }
115	            throw ToolError(message: error.localizedDescription + " " + sentence)
116	        }
117	    }
118	
119	    /// What a tool call's refusal adds when an installed ffmpeg could have
120	    /// converted the file but the policy is `ask`, which a call never asks
121	    /// (spec §11 MC-5); nil otherwise. Both refusals that would have gone on
122	    /// to the ffmpeg step count: AVFoundation's (`ImportError`) and, for a
123	    /// WebM or Matroska file, a codec the built-in copy cannot carry
124	    /// (`ContainerRewrapError.unsupported`, spec §11 #216-R).
125	    static func neverAsksSentence(for error: any Error, url: URL) -> String? {
126	        let invites =

139	    /// `import_captions` — File ▸ Import Captions… (`CaptionImporter`, which
140	    /// also carries the reasoning for why a caption is a text clip).
141	    ///
142	    /// Runs on the main thread like every other op tool: parsing an SRT is
143	    /// reading a text file, not probing a movie, so there is nothing to wait
144	    /// for and nothing to keep off main.
145	    ///
146	    /// The result reports what was SKIPPED as well as what landed — a
147	    /// caption file with three malformed entries would otherwise import
148	    /// silently short, and a model has no other way to see it.
149	    func importCaptions(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> String {
150	        let document = try target(a)
151	        let path = try requiredString(a, "path")
152	        let url = URL(fileURLWithPath: (path as NSString).expandingTildeInPath)
153	        guard FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: url.path) else {
154	            throw ToolError(message: "No file at \(url.path)")
155	        }
156	        var track: UInt32?
157	        if a["track"] != nil, !(a["track"] is NSNull) {
158	            track = try trackArg(a, "track", document).id
159	        }
160	        let plan: CaptionImporter.Plan
161	        do {
162	            // The EDITED project, like its three siblings (the File-menu
163	            // importer, `Transcriber` and the `transcribe` tool): the ops
164	            // this plan produces are addressed to whatever nest is open, so
165	            // reading the document here would measure a placement against
166	            // the timeline and land the clips inside the nest.
167	            plan = try CaptionImporter.plan(for: url, in: document.editedProject, track: track)
168	        } catch {
169	            throw ToolError(message: error.localizedDescription)
170	        }
171	        var fields: [String: Any] = ["captions": plan.clips, "cues": plan.cues]
172	        if let name = plan.trackName { fields["track_name"] = name }
173	        if plan.trimmed > 0 { fields["trimmed"] = plan.trimmed }
174	        if !plan.problems.isEmpty {
175	            fields["skipped"] = plan.problems.map { $0.description }
176	        }
177	        return try editResult(document, "Import Captions", plan.ops, fields)
178	    }

182	    /// `consolidate_media` — File ▸ Consolidate Media…
183	    /// (`EditorViewController+Consolidate.swift`; `MediaConsolidator` owns
184	    /// the plan, the copying and the four traps).
185	    ///
186	    /// The copy runs on the main thread, where every non-`offMainTools`
187	    /// handler runs: it is `FileManager` work with no waiting in it, so the
188	    /// only cost is that the app's own UI is unresponsive while a large
189	    /// library copies — the connection is served on the server thread and
190	    /// stays live throughout. The app's sheet does the same work on a
191	    /// background queue because there is a person watching that one.
192	    func consolidateMedia(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> String {
193	        let document = try target(a)
194	        let plan: MediaConsolidator.Plan
195	        do {
196	            plan = try MediaConsolidator.plan(for: document)
197	        } catch let error as MediaConsolidator.ConsolidateError {
198	            guard case .untitled = error else {
199	                throw ToolError(message: error.localizedDescription)
200	            }
201	            throw ToolError(
202	                message: error.localizedDescription + " Call save_project with a path first.")
203	        } catch {
204	            throw ToolError(message: error.localizedDescription)
205	        }
206	        // Already self-contained is not an error — it is the state the
207	        // caller asked for, and `editResult` would report the empty op list
208	        // as a refusal.
209	        guard !plan.isEmpty else {
210	            return try jsonResult([
211	                "ok": true, "copied": 0, "directory": plan.directory.path,
212	                "missing": plan.missing,
213	                "note": "Every file this project can find is already inside the package.",
214	                "project": summary(document),
215	            ])
216	        }
217	        let outcome = MediaConsolidator.run(plan)
218	        // Creating `media/` inside the package moves the package's own
219	        // modification date, which NSDocument reads as another application
220	        // having changed the file and refuses every later save over. Told
221	        // unconditionally, since a failed run may still have made it.
222	        document.packageContentsDidChangeOnDisk()
223	        guard !outcome.ops.isEmpty else {
224	            throw ToolError(message: outcome.summary)
225	        }
226	        var fields: [String: Any] = [
227	            "copied": outcome.copied, "bytes": Int(outcome.bytes),
228	            "directory": plan.directory.path, "summary": outcome.summary,
229	        ]
230	        if !outcome.failures.isEmpty { fields["failures"] = outcome.failures }
231	        if !outcome.missing.isEmpty { fields["missing"] = outcome.missing }
232	        let result = try editResult(document, "Consolidate Media", outcome.ops, fields)
233	        document.generateCaches()
234	        return result
235	    }

239	    /// `add_media` — the op behind `import_media`, exposed for parity with
240	    /// spec §6. It takes the descriptor a probe produced (the `media[]`
241	    /// element of §5.2 minus its id), so unless you are replaying a project's
242	    /// own JSON, call `import_media` and let the host probe.
243	    func addMedia(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> String {
244	        let document = try target(a)
245	        guard let object = a["descriptor"] as? [String: Any] else {
246	            throw ToolError(
247	                message: "descriptor must be a JSON object — the media[] element of the project "
248	                    + "JSON minus its id. import_media probes a file and builds it for you.")
249	        }
250	        let descriptor = try mediaDescriptor(object)
251	        let expected = document.project.snapshot.nextId
252	        let before = try performGroupedEdit(
253	            document, "Add Media", [.addMedia(descriptor: descriptor)])
254	        let added = ProjectSnapshot.addedMedia(from: before, to: document.project.snapshot)
255	        document.generateCaches()
256	        return try jsonResult(
257	            [
258	                "ok": true, "media": Int(added.first ?? expected), "path": descriptor.path,
259	                "project": summary(document),
260	            ])
261	    }

263	    /// A `media[]` element minus its id, under the model's own key names.
264	    /// Everything but `path` has a default, so a descriptor for a still is
265	    /// `{"path": …, "kind": "image", "width": …, "height": …}`.
266	    private func mediaDescriptor(_ object: [String: Any]) throws -> MediaDescriptor {
267	        let allowed: Set<String> = [
268	            "path", "bookmark", "kind", "duration", "width", "height", "fps", "has_video",
269	            "has_audio", "has_alpha", "original", "color", "cursor",
270	        ]
271	        let unknown = object.keys.filter { !allowed.contains($0) }.sorted()
272	        if let first = unknown.first {
273	            throw ToolError(
274	                message: "Unknown descriptor key \"\(first)\" — allowed keys are "
275	                    + allowed.sorted().joined(separator: ", ") + ".")
276	        }
277	        let path = try requiredString(object, "path")
278	        let kind = try enumArg(object, "kind", MediaKind.self) ?? .video
279	        var fps = Fps.thirty
280	        if let array = object["fps"] as? [Any] {
281	            fps = try fpsPair(array, "descriptor.fps")
282	        } else if object["fps"] != nil, !(object["fps"] is NSNull) {
283	            throw ToolError(
284	                message: "descriptor.fps must be [numerator, denominator], e.g. [30000, 1001].")
285	        }
286	        return MediaDescriptor(
287	            path: (path as NSString).expandingTildeInPath,
288	            bookmark: try stringArg(object, "bookmark"),
289	            kind: kind,
290	            duration: Ticks(try intArg(object, "duration") ?? 0),
291	            width: try intArg(object, "width") ?? 0,
292	            height: try intArg(object, "height") ?? 0,
293	            fps: fps,
294	            hasVideo: try boolArg(object, "has_video") ?? (kind == .video || kind == .image),
295	            hasAudio: try boolArg(object, "has_audio") ?? (kind == .audio),
296	            hasAlpha: try boolArg(object, "has_alpha") ?? false,
297	            original: try mediaOriginal(object["original"]),
298	            color: try mediaColor(object["color"]),
299	            cursor: try mediaCursor(object["cursor"]))
300	    }

302	    /// A descriptor's `color` (spec §11 GR-16): `{log?, gamut?, lut?,
303	    /// detected?, pq?}`, or nil when absent or null. Each wrong shape and word
304	    /// is refused by name; what the setting may HOLD is the core's to refuse
305	    /// (`add_media` holds it to `set_media_color`'s rules).
306	    private func mediaColor(_ raw: Any?) throws -> MediaColor? {
307	        guard let raw = raw, !(raw is NSNull) else { return nil }
308	        guard let object = raw as? [String: Any] else {
309	            throw ToolError(
310	                message: "descriptor.color must be a JSON object {log, gamut?} or {lut} — the "
311	                    + "file's Camera Log, as set_media_color takes it, plus detected — and "
312	                    + "pq, a PQ file's peak as get_project shows it.")
313	        }
314	        let allowed: Set<String> = ["log", "gamut", "lut", "detected", "pq"]
315	        if let first = object.keys.filter({ !allowed.contains($0) }).sorted().first {
316	            throw ToolError(
317	                message: "Unknown color key \"\(first)\" — allowed keys are "
318	                    + allowed.sorted().joined(separator: ", ") + ".")
319	        }
320	        var color = MediaColor(detected: try boolArg(object, "detected") ?? false)
321	        color.log = try enumArg(object, "log", LogCurve.self, label: "descriptor.color.log")
322	        color.gamut = try enumArg(
323	            object, "gamut", CameraGamut.self, label: "descriptor.color.gamut")
324	        if object["lut"] != nil, !(object["lut"] is NSNull) {
325	            color.lut = try idArg(object, "lut")
326	        }
327	        color.pq = try mediaPQ(object["pq"])
328	        return color
329	    }

331	    /// A descriptor's `color.pq` (spec §11 HD-12): `{file?, from?, peak?}`,
332	    /// a PQ file's HDR10 peak as `media[]` stores it, or nil when absent or
333	    /// null. Each wrong shape and word is refused by name; the range and the
334	    /// pairing of `from` with `file` are the core's to refuse.
335	    private func mediaPQ(_ raw: Any?) throws -> PQColor? {
336	        guard let raw = raw, !(raw is NSNull) else { return nil }
337	        guard let object = raw as? [String: Any] else {
338	            throw ToolError(
339	                message: "descriptor.color.pq must be a JSON object {file?, from?, peak?} — a "
340	                    + "PQ file's HDR10 peak as get_project shows it.")
341	        }
342	        let allowed: Set<String> = ["file", "from", "peak"]
343	        if let first = object.keys.filter({ !allowed.contains($0) }).sorted().first {
344	            throw ToolError(
345	                message: "Unknown color.pq key \"\(first)\" — allowed keys are "
346	                    + allowed.sorted().joined(separator: ", ") + ".")
347	        }
348	        var pq = PQColor(file: try peakArg(object, "file"), peak: try peakArg(object, "peak"))
349	        pq.from = try enumArg(object, "from", PeakSource.self, label: "descriptor.color.pq.from")
350	        return pq
351	    }

353	    /// One of `color.pq`'s peaks, a whole number of cd/m² that fits the field.
354	    private func peakArg(_ object: [String: Any], _ key: String) throws -> UInt32? {
355	        guard let value = try intArg(object, key) else { return nil }
356	        guard let peak = UInt32(exactly: value) else {
357	            throw ToolError(
358	                message: "descriptor.color.pq.\(key) must be a whole number of cd/m² "
359	                    + "(got \(value)).")
360	        }
361	        return peak
362	    }

367	        guard let raw = raw, !(raw is NSNull) else { return nil }

369	            throw ToolError(

391	    /// bookmark?, in_picture}`, or nil when absent or null. A wrong shape, an

396	        guard let raw = raw, !(raw is NSNull) else { return nil }

398	            throw ToolError(
399	                message: "descriptor.cursor must be a JSON object {path, bookmark?, in_picture} "
400	                    + "— the cursor file recorded beside the movie.")
401	        }
402	        let allowed: Set<String> = ["path", "bookmark", "in_picture"]
403	        if let first = object.keys.filter({ !allowed.contains($0) }).sorted().first {
404	            throw ToolError(

421	    // MARK: - Relinking and removing

423	    /// `relink_media` — Relink… (`RelinkSheetController`, and the Media tab's
424	    /// row menu, both through `ProjectDocument.relinkMedia`). The new file
425	    /// is probed as `import_media` probes it and the descriptor fills the
426	    /// op's `probe` (spec §11, #63), so the entry takes the file's duration,
427	    /// size, rate and flags, a file of another kind is refused in the core's
428	    /// sentence, and a clip past a shorter file's end is held to it.
429	    ///
430	    /// **Runs on the server thread** (`AgentServer.offMainTools`), for
431	    /// `importMedia`'s reason: the probe's completion arrives on main. The
432	    /// path stored is the DESCRIPTOR's (an ffmpeg rewrap stores the `.mov`),
433	    /// and so is the bookmark unless the caller gave one for that same file:
434	    /// a caller's bookmark of the original beside a rewrapped path would
435	    /// make `mediaURL`, which resolves the bookmark first, open the file the
436	    /// record does not name.
437	    func relinkMedia(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> String {
438	        let (document, media) = try onMain {
439	            let document = try self.target(a)
440	            return (document, try self.mediaArg(a, "media", document))
441	        }
442	        let path = try requiredString(a, "path")
443	        let url = URL(fileURLWithPath: (path as NSString).expandingTildeInPath)
444	        guard FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: url.path) else {
445	            throw ToolError(message: "No file at \(url.path)")
446	        }
447	        let given = try stringArg(a, "bookmark")
448	        let descriptor = MediaImporter.relinkProbe(try probe(url), current: media)  // CU-38 (a)
449	        let bookmark = descriptor.path == url.path ? given ?? descriptor.bookmark
450	            : descriptor.bookmark
451	        var fields: [String: Any] = [
452	            "media": Int(media.id), "path": descriptor.path,
453	            "kind": descriptor.kind.rawValue, "duration": descriptor.duration,
454	            "width": descriptor.width, "height": descriptor.height,
455	            "fps": [descriptor.fps.num, descriptor.fps.den],
456	            "has_video": descriptor.hasVideo, "has_audio": descriptor.hasAudio,
457	            "has_alpha": descriptor.hasAlpha,
458	        ]
459	        // The new original, when the file was copied or converted (#228-O, #233).
460	        if let original = descriptor.original { fields["original"] = original.path }
461	        return try onMain {
462	            let result = try self.editResult(
463	                document, "Relink Media",
464	                [
465	                    .relinkMedia(
466	                        media: media.id, path: descriptor.path, bookmark: bookmark,
467	                        probe: descriptor)
468	                ],
469	                fields)
470	            document.generateCaches()
471	            return result
472	        }
473	    }

468	    /// A path in the one spelling both sides of a `project` comparison can be
469	    /// written in.

471	    /// Matching `fileURL.path` against the caller's string exactly is wrong
472	    /// twice over. A caller may legitimately spell the same file
473	    /// `~/Movies/x.framejob`, `/tmp/x.framejob` or `/private/tmp/x.framejob` —
474	    /// and, the case that actually bit, AppKit's own save machinery can hand
475	    /// `fileURL` back in the OTHER spelling of that last pair, so a path that
476	    /// addressed the document for twenty calls suddenly answers "No open
477	    /// project is at …". `standardizedFileURL` folds `.`, `..` and doubled or
478	    /// trailing slashes; `resolvingSymlinksInPath` folds `/tmp` ⇄
479	    /// `/private/tmp` (and `/var`, `/etc`) whether or not the file exists yet.
480	    /// Two paths only collide here when they name the same file, which is the
481	    /// answer wanted.

483	        URL(fileURLWithPath: (path as NSString).expandingTildeInPath)
484	            .standardizedFileURL.resolvingSymlinksInPath().path

487	    /// The document a call targets: `project` (a path, as `get_project`
488	    /// reports it) when given, else the frontmost document, else the most
489	    /// recently created one. Main thread only.
490	    ///
491	    /// **Pitfall.** `NSDocumentController.currentDocument` is the document of
492	    /// `NSApp.mainWindow`, and an application that is not the ACTIVE
493	    /// application has no main window — which is the normal state for an
494	    /// agent-driven session, where nobody ever clicks the app. Falling
495	    /// straight through to `documents.first` there silently targets the
496	    /// OLDEST open project, so `new_project` followed by an edit edits some
497	    /// other document and says nothing. `NSApp.orderedDocuments` follows the
498	    /// app's own front-to-back window order, which `showWindows()` maintains
499	    /// whether or not the app is active, so it answers correctly in both
500	    /// states; `documents.last` is the last resort for a windowless document
501	    /// (the agent can make one), where newest is the better guess than
502	    /// oldest.
503	    func target(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> ProjectDocument {
504	        let document = try targetDocument(a)
505	        // The scope is validated HERE, at the one gate every handler passes
506	        // through before it reads a single id, because the order of the two
507	        // refusals is part of the contract (`core/src/scope.rs`): a scope
508	        // naming no nest is answered by name, ahead of anything else, since
509	        // it is the argument that decides which document the caller thinks
510	        // it is editing. Doing it in the readers instead would make the
511	        // message depend on which argument a handler happens to read first —
512	        // `trim_start`'s `clip`, `close_gap`'s `at` — and would leave the
513	        // handlers that read no ids at all validating nothing.
514	        try checkCallScope(document)
515	        return document
516	    }

518	    private func targetDocument(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> ProjectDocument {
519	        if let pinned = callDocument { return try pinnedTarget(pinned, a) }
520	        assert(Thread.isMainThread)
521	        let documents = openProjects()
522	        if let wanted = try stringArg(a, "project") {
523	            let path = (wanted as NSString).expandingTildeInPath
524	            let canonical = Self.canonical(wanted)
525	            guard
526	                let match = documents.first(where: {
527	                    guard let open = Self.path(of: $0) else { return false }
528	                    return open == path || Self.canonical(open) == canonical
529	                })
530	            else {
531	                throw ToolError(
532	                    message: "No open project is at \(path). get_project reports the open "
533	                        + "project's path; open_project opens another.")
534	            }
535	            return match
536	        }
537	        if let current = NSDocumentController.shared.currentDocument as? ProjectDocument {
538	            return current
539	        }
540	        if let ordered = NSApp.orderedDocuments.first(where: { $0 is ProjectDocument })
541	            as? ProjectDocument
542	        {
543	            return ordered
544	        }
545	        guard let newest = documents.last else {
546	            throw ToolError(
547	                message: "No project is open. Call open_project or new_project first.")
548	        }
549	        return newest
550	    }

561	    /// The one-line description of a project every result carries, so a model
562	    /// never has to call `get_project` just to see what its edit did.
563	    func summary(_ document: ProjectDocument) -> [String: Any] {
564	        let snapshot = document.project.snapshot
565	        let canvas = snapshot.canvas
566	        // missing_media rides on EVERY summary, not just get_project's: the
567	        // moment a caller most needs to know a file is gone is the open that
568	        // just surfaced it, and open_project answers with a summary. The key
569	        // is omitted when nothing is missing so a healthy project stays terse.
570	        var result: [String: Any] = [
571	            "name": document.displayName ?? "Untitled",
572	            "path": Self.path(of: document) ?? NSNull(),
573	            "width": canvas.width,
574	            "height": canvas.height,
575	            "fps": [canvas.fps.num, canvas.fps.den],
576	            "duration": document.project.duration,
577	            "playhead": document.playhead,
578	            "tracks": snapshot.tracks.count,
579	            "clips": snapshot.clips.count,
580	            "markers": snapshot.markers.count,
581	            "media": snapshot.media.count,
582	            "selection": document.selection.sorted().map { Int($0) },
583	            "unsaved_changes": document.isDocumentEdited,
584	        ]
585	        let missing = document.missingMedia.map { Int($0.id) }.sorted()
586	        if !missing.isEmpty { result["missing_media"] = missing }

590	    // MARK: - Editing
591	
592	    /// Applies `ops` as ONE undo step and returns the snapshot from BEFORE
593	    /// the edit (which is what names the ids it created).
594	    ///
595	    /// The ops are tried on the handle FIRST, purely — `ReelProject.applying`
596	    /// mutates nothing — because `ProjectDocument.applyEdit` answers the two
597	    /// failure cases with UI: an identity edit beeps and an invalid one puts
598	    /// up an alert sheet. Both are wrong on a dispatched-to-main tool call:
599	    /// the model needs the message, and a modal would block the connection.
600	    /// The trial costs a handle and no pixels (spec §5.5).
601	    ///
602	    /// The commit then goes through `ProjectDocument.performGroupedEdit`,
603	    /// whose explicit `beginUndoGrouping`/`endUndoGrouping` + flush is the
604	    /// off-event pattern (app/CLAUDE.md): an undo registration made outside an
605	    /// AppKit event otherwise lands in an implicit group AppKit never closes,
606	    /// silently merging every agent edit into one undo step.
607	    ///
608	    /// **This is where the call's scope is stamped onto its ops**, and the
609	    /// one place: every tool that edits ends here or in `editResult` above
610	    /// it, including the two composites that call it directly, so no handler
611	    /// has to remember. The rule is `AgentServer+Scope.addressed`, which
612	    /// mirrors `ProjectDocument.addressed(_:)` — and it has to be stamped
613	    /// BEFORE the trial below, not only at the commit, or a scoped edit would
614	    /// be tried against the wrong container and reported as a refusal it
615	    /// never suffered. With no scope anywhere it is the identity, which is
616	    /// what makes an unscoped call byte-for-byte the call it always was.
617	    ///
618	    /// It is also where the ops an inherited scope may NOT send are refused,
619	    /// for the same reason: this is the one place every editing tool passes
620	    /// through. `checkDocumentLevelTicks` is that rule and argues it.
621	    @discardableResult
622	    func performGroupedEdit(
623	        _ document: ProjectDocument, _ actionName: String, _ ops: [ReelOp]
624	    ) throws -> ProjectSnapshot {
625	        // `addressed` sends a document-level op UNSCOPED out of a scope it
626	        // inherited, which is right for five of the seven and a wrong
627	        // PLACEMENT for the two that carry a tick — a marker written from
628	        // inside a nest is measured from the nest's zero and lands elsewhere
629	        // on the timeline. Refused before the stamp, beside the rule it
630	        // guards (`AgentServer+Scope.swift`).
631	        try checkDocumentLevelTicks(ops, document)
632	        let ops = addressed(ops, document)
633	        let handle = document.project
634	        let before = handle.snapshot
635	        do {
636	            // Two non-applied arms, two answers, and since D2·2 this says
637	            // which (spec §5.5). Both are still "the project did not change"
638	            // and still in-band; what stopped is the GUESSING.
639	            switch try document.project.applying(ops) {
640	            case .applied: break
641	            case .identity:  // Only that — no rule the caller did not break.
642	                throw ToolError(message: "\(actionName) made no change: the project is "
643	                    + "already in that state.")
644	            case .refused(let refusal):  // The rule's own sentence, and WHICH op.
645	                throw ToolError(
646	                    message: "\(actionName) was refused at \(refusal.op): \(refusal.reason)")
647	            }
648	        } catch let error as ToolError {
649	            throw error
650	        } catch {
651	            throw ToolError(message: error.localizedDescription)
652	        }
653	        document.performGroupedEdit(actionName, ops)
654	        // **The trial promised a change; this is where the promise is
655	        // checked**, and it is one pointer comparison because `applyEdit`
656	        // replaces the handle only when the core answered with a new project.
657	        //
658	        // Nothing should ever be able to fire it: the commit applies the same
659	        // ops to the same handle the trial just succeeded against. It is here
660	        // because the ONE way the two can disagree is over the addressing —
661	        // this side stamps a scope, `ProjectDocument.addressed(_:)` stamps
662	        // one too, and a disagreement between them is invisible from a tool
663	        // result (measured, road map 2's phase 9: an explicit `scope` sent
664	        // while a DIFFERENT nest was open in the window was re-addressed to
665	        // the open one, failed in the core, put its message in a sheet the
666	        // agent cannot see, and the tool answered `ok`). That defect is
667	        // CLOSED — `addressed(_:)` now keeps a scope an op already carries,
668	        // so an explicit scope outranks the open view — and this guard is the
669	        // defence that survives it, because the two stamps still live in two
670	        // files. A tool that lies about an edit is worse than one that
671	        // refuses, so this refuses.
672	        guard document.project !== handle else {
673	            throw ToolError(
674	                message: "\(actionName) was accepted when it was tried but the document did "
675	                    + "not change, so nothing was edited. The ops as the document sent them "
676	                    + "were addressed differently from the ops that were tried — check the "
677	                    + "scope against what set_scope has open — and the project is untouched.")
678	        }
679	        return before
680	    }
681	
682	    /// The canonical op-handler tail: `performGroupedEdit`, then the standard
683	    /// result — `ok`, whatever the handler wants to add, the ids the edit
684	    /// created, and the project summary.
685	    func editResult(
686	        _ document: ProjectDocument, _ actionName: String, _ ops: [ReelOp],
687	        _ fields: [String: Any] = [:]
688	    ) throws -> String {
689	        // A scoped edit changes nothing the `project` summary counts, so
690	        // without this an `ok` from inside a nest is indistinguishable from
691	        // an `ok` on the timeline that did nothing visible. What says WHERE
692	        // it landed is read off the ops as `addressed` STAMPS them and never
693	        // off the VIEW — `AgentServer+Scope.scopeLanding` is that account and
694	        // argues it, mixed edits included — and it is taken BEFORE the edit,
695	        // because how a call was addressed is a fact about the call. Nothing
696	        // is added with no scope anywhere, so no existing result grew a key.
697	        let landing = scopeLanding(ops, document)
698	        let before = try performGroupedEdit(document, actionName, ops)
699	        var result: [String: Any] = ["ok": true]
700	        result.merge(fields) { _, new in new }
701	        result.merge(Self.created(from: before, to: document.project.snapshot)) { _, new in new }
702	        result.merge(SpeedAudioDrop.answerFields(from: before, to: document.project.snapshot)) {
703	            _, new in new
704	        }
705	        result.merge(landing) { _, new in new }
706	        result["project"] = summary(document)
707	        return try jsonResult(result)
708	    }
709	
710	    /// The ids an edit ADDED, by kind. A split, a duplicate, a freeze frame
711	    /// and a detach all mint clips the caller then wants to name, and there is
712	    /// one FFI entry point for every op (spec §11) — so no op returns an id
713	    /// and the difference of the two snapshots is how they are reported.
714	    ///
715	    /// **Clips and tracks are counted across every container**, the
716	    /// timeline's and every nest's, which is `Project::every_clip()`'s rule
717	    /// in Swift and is what road map 2's phase 9 needed: a scoped `split`
718	    /// mints its two halves INSIDE a nest and a scoped `add_track` mints its
719	    /// track there, so a diff of the top level alone answered with nothing at
720	    /// all and left the caller to find them by reading the whole project
721	    /// back. Markers and media are deliberately still the top level's: a nest
722	    /// has neither, and both lists ARE the document's.
723	    ///
724	    /// It leaves every unscoped clip answer exactly as it was — `nest` moves
725	    /// its clips WHOLE, ids and all (`edit_nest.rs`), so the only new clip is
726	    /// still the nest clip it minted, and it comes first because the
727	    /// timeline's clips are concatenated ahead of the nests'. It does change
728	    /// ONE unscoped answer, and for the better: `nest` mints a fresh TRACK
729	    /// per source track inside the nest, and those ids — real ids in the
730	    /// document's one number space, which `set_track` and `move_track` can
731	    /// now name through a scope — used to be reported nowhere.
732	    static func created(from before: ProjectSnapshot, to after: ProjectSnapshot)
733	        -> [String: Any] {
734	        var result: [String: Any] = [:]
735	        func added<T: Identifiable>(_ old: [T], _ new: [T]) -> [Int] where T.ID == UInt32 {
736	            let existing = Set(old.map { $0.id })
737	            return new.map { $0.id }.filter { !existing.contains($0) }.map { Int($0) }
738	        }
739	        let clips = added(
740	            before.clips + before.nests.flatMap { $0.clips },
741	            after.clips + after.nests.flatMap { $0.clips })
742	        if !clips.isEmpty { result["new_clips"] = clips }
743	        let tracks = added(
744	            before.tracks + before.nests.flatMap { $0.tracks },
745	            after.tracks + after.nests.flatMap { $0.tracks })
746	        if !tracks.isEmpty { result["new_tracks"] = tracks }
747	        let markers = added(before.markers, after.markers)
748	        if !markers.isEmpty { result["new_markers"] = markers }
749	        let media = added(before.media, after.media)
750	        if !media.isEmpty { result["new_media"] = media }
751	        return result
752	    }
753	
754	    // MARK: - Result encoding
755	
756	    func callResult(content: [[String: Any]], isError: Bool) throws -> String {
757	        let data = try JSONSerialization.data(
758	            withJSONObject: ["content": content, "isError": isError])
759	        return String(decoding: data, as: UTF8.self)
760	    }
761	
762	    func jsonResult(_ object: [String: Any]) throws -> String {
763	        let data = try JSONSerialization.data(withJSONObject: object)
764	        return try callResult(
765	            content: [["type": "text", "text": String(decoding: data, as: UTF8.self)]],
766	            isError: false)
767	    }
768	
769	    private func errorResult(_ message: String) -> String {
770	        let content: [[String: Any]] = [["type": "text", "text": message]]
771	        let fallback = #"{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"tool failed"}],"isError":true}"#
772	        guard
773	            let data = try? JSONSerialization.data(
774	                withJSONObject: ["content": content, "isError": true])
775	        else { return fallback }
776	        return String(decoding: data, as: UTF8.self)
777	    }
778	}

3	/// Where the agent's output tools write: `render_frame`, `export`,
4	/// `export_captions`, `render_graphic`'s sheet and `snapshot_ui` all take a
5	/// `path`, and every one of them names its file through `destinationURL`
6	/// here, refuses a path whose folder does not exist through `requireFolder`,
7	/// and the three that may omit `path` refuse an empty one through
8	/// `nonEmptyOutputPath` and name a temporary file through `temporaryOutput`.
9	extension AgentServer {
10	
11	    /// An output path as the tools take one: `~` expanded, and the extension
12	    /// the format actually needs (a `.framejob` package without its extension
13	    /// is not a package, and an `.mp4` written to a name ending `.mov` claims
14	    /// a container it does not have).
15	    ///
16	    /// A WRONG extension is REPLACED, not appended to. Appending is what
17	    /// turned an export to `final.mov` with an MP4-container preset into
18	    /// `final.mov.mp4` — a file at neither the path the caller asked for nor
19	    /// one they would guess. Every caller reports the URL this returns, so
20	    /// the substitution is never silent.
21	    /// The extensions `destinationURL` will REPLACE: the containers this app
22	    /// writes, its own package, and the media extensions a caller is most
23	    /// likely to type out of habit. Everything else is part of the name.
24	    ///
25	    /// `srt` and `vtt` joined the list when `export_captions` landed, because
26	    /// they are containers this app writes. `export_captions` no longer reads
27	    /// this set (spec §11 #43): it replaces only
28	    /// `CaptionExporter.knownExtensions`, through `captionDestinationURL`, as
29	    /// the save panel does. The two stay here for the other tools, so a still
30	    /// or a movie named `talk.srt` is renamed rather than doubled.
31	    ///
32	    /// The five image containers joined it in road map 2's phase 7a, on the
33	    /// same terms and for two reasons rather than one. The new one:
34	    /// `render_frame` takes a `path` and a `format` now (`FrameWriter`), so
35	    /// `render_frame {path: "shot.jpg", format: "png"}` would have written
36	    /// `shot.jpg.png`. The old one is a REAL BUG this fixes rather than
37	    /// prevents — `gif` has been a container this app writes since M3's image
38	    /// sequences, and without it `export {path: "loop.gif", preset: "apng"}`
39	    /// writes `loop.gif.png` today. Both spellings of JPEG are here because a
40	    /// person types both; `heif` is NOT, because this app never writes one
41	    /// (`FrameWriter.Format.heic` is `UTType.heic` for the measured reason
42	    /// recorded there), so a file called `scene.heif` keeps its name.
43	    private static let replaceableExtensions: Set<String> = [
44	        "mov", "mp4", "m4v", "m4a", "mp3", "wav", "aif", "aiff", "caf", "framejob", "srt", "vtt",
45	        "png", "jpg", "jpeg", "heic", "gif",
46	    ]
47	
48	    static func destinationURL(_ path: String, extension ext: String) -> URL {
49	        destinationURL(path, extension: ext, replacing: replaceableExtensions)
50	    }
51	
52	    /// `destinationURL` over a caller's own set of replaceable extensions:
53	    /// `export_captions` passes `CaptionExporter.knownExtensions` (#43).
54	    static func destinationURL(
55	        _ path: String, extension ext: String, replacing replaceable: Set<String>
56	    ) -> URL {
57	        let expanded = (path as NSString).expandingTildeInPath
58	        let url = URL(fileURLWithPath: expanded)
59	        let current = url.pathExtension
60	        if current.lowercased() == ext.lowercased() { return url }
61	        // Only a KNOWN container extension is replaced. A "looks like an
62	        // extension" heuristic is not good enough: it turns "Talk v1.2" into
63	        // "Talk v1.mp4", silently dropping a character the caller typed on
64	        // purpose. Anything not on this list is treated as part of the name
65	        // and the extension is appended to it.
66	        let base = replaceable.contains(current.lowercased())
67	            ? url.deletingPathExtension() : url
68	        return base.appendingPathExtension(ext)
69	    }
70	
71	    /// `url` when its folder already exists; refused BY NAME when it does
72	    /// not. A tool that created directories would answer a mistyped path by
73	    /// scattering empty ones, so every output tool takes the folder as given.
74	    static func requireFolder(of url: URL) throws -> URL {
75	        let folder = url.deletingLastPathComponent()
76	        var isDirectory: ObjCBool = false
77	        guard FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: folder.path, isDirectory: &isDirectory),
78	            isDirectory.boolValue
79	        else {
80	            throw ToolError(message: "There is no folder at \(folder.path) to write into.")
81	        }
82	        return url
83	    }
84	
85	    /// A temporary file for a tool whose caller omitted `path`: `stem`, a
86	    /// short random suffix so two calls never collide, and `ext`.
87	    static func temporaryOutput(_ stem: String, extension ext: String) -> URL {
88	        FileManager.default.temporaryDirectory
89	            .appendingPathComponent("\(stem)-\(UUID().uuidString.prefix(8)).\(ext)")
90	    }

3	/// The agent's media tools: the three `media` rows of spec §6's op table plus
4	/// `import_media`, the one an agent actually wants — `add_media` takes a
5	/// descriptor somebody has to have probed, and probing files is the host's job
6	/// (spec §7.7).
7	extension AgentServer {
8	
9	    // MARK: - Importing
10	
11	    /// `import_media` — File ▸ Add Media… and every Finder drop
12	    /// (`ProjectDocument.importMedia`): probe the file, then `add_media`.
13	    /// With `set_video {look: {kind: "lut", media}}` after it, it mirrors the
14	    /// Look section's Import LUT… (`EditorViewController.importLUT`, GR-8).
15	    ///
16	    /// **Runs on the server thread** (`AgentServer.offMainTools`).
17	    /// `MediaImporter.probe`'s completion is delivered on the MAIN thread, so
18	    /// a main-thread wait for it would deadlock; waiting here leaves main free
19	    /// to deliver it, exactly as `ProjectDocument.readMediaFile` waits on
20	    /// NSDocument's background read queue.
21	    ///
22	    /// **The new media id is the project's `next_id` from BEFORE the op** —
23	    /// the documented contract (`ReelOp.addMedia`), because there is one FFI
24	    /// entry point for every op (spec §11) and it returns a project, not a
25	    /// value. The id is read off the snapshot first and cross-checked against
26	    /// what the edit actually added.
27	    func importMedia(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> String {
28	        let path = try requiredString(a, "path")
29	        let url = URL(fileURLWithPath: (path as NSString).expandingTildeInPath)
30	        guard FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: url.path) else {
31	            throw ToolError(message: "No file at \(url.path)")
32	        }
33	        let document = try onMain { try self.target(a) }
34	        let descriptor = try probe(url)
35	        return try onMain {
36	            let expected = document.project.snapshot.nextId
37	            let before = try self.performGroupedEdit(
38	                document, "Add Media", [.addMedia(descriptor: descriptor)])
39	            let added = ProjectSnapshot.addedMedia(from: before, to: document.project.snapshot)
40	            document.generateCaches()
41	            var result: [String: Any] = [
42	                "ok": true,
43	                "media": Int(added.first ?? expected),
44	                // The DESCRIPTOR's path, not the argument's: an ffmpeg-assisted
45	                // import rewraps the file and the model stores the conversion,
46	                // so echoing what was asked for would answer `.mkv` about an
47	                // entry that is really a `.mov`. The rule generalises — the
48	                // answer must describe what landed in the project.
49	                "path": descriptor.path,
50	                "kind": descriptor.kind.rawValue,
51	                "duration": descriptor.duration,
52	                "width": descriptor.width,
53	                "height": descriptor.height,
54	                "fps": [descriptor.fps.num, descriptor.fps.den],
55	                "has_video": descriptor.hasVideo,
56	                "has_audio": descriptor.hasAudio,
57	                "has_alpha": descriptor.hasAlpha,
58	            ]
59	            // A copy's or an ffmpeg conversion's original (spec §11 #228-O,
60	            // #233): the file the caller named, which the media is named after.
61	            if let original = descriptor.original { result["original"] = original.path }
62	            result["note"] =
63	                descriptor.kind == .lut
64	                ? "The LUT is in the project's media list. It is never placed as a clip: apply it "
65	                    + "as a look with set_video {clips, patch: {look: {kind: \"lut\", media: "
66	                    + "\(Int(added.first ?? expected))}}}."
67	                : "The file is in the project's media list but not on the timeline yet — place "
68	                    + "it with add_clip {track, media, at}."
69	            result["project"] = self.summary(document)
70	            return try self.jsonResult(result)

74	    /// The longest one import's own runs can take (spec §11 #227; the time it
75	    /// queues behind another import's conversion is not counted): the opt-in
76	    /// ffmpeg step's own bound, both attempts (`FFmpegRewrap.longestAssist`:
77	    /// the plan, the frame check, the encoder query, a VP9 copy and then its
78	    /// re-encode, and `run`'s grace on each of those five runs), plus three
79	    /// header probes (`MediaImporter.probeTimeout`: the source, the copy and
80	    /// the re-encode). `import_media` and `relink_media` both wait this long.
81	    static let probeCeiling: TimeInterval =
82	        FFmpegRewrap.longestAssist + 3 * MediaImporter.probeTimeout
83	
84	    /// Probes one file and waits for the answer. MUST run off the main thread
85	    /// — see `importMedia` — and gives up only after `probeCeiling`: a file
86	    /// AVFoundation cannot read may be converted by ffmpeg first
87	    /// (`FFmpegRewrap.assist`), which legitimately takes as long as
88	    /// `FFmpegRewrap.longestAssist`, so a shorter wait would answer a
89	    /// timeout while the conversion is still running. A tool call never
90	    /// asks the conversion question (spec §11 MC-5), so it passes
91	    /// `mayAsk: false`, and a refusal ffmpeg could have helped names the
92	    /// setting (`neverAsksSentence`).
93	    private func probe(_ url: URL) throws -> MediaDescriptor {
94	        guard !Thread.isMainThread else {
95	            throw ToolError(message: "Probing cannot run on the main thread.")
96	        }
97	        let semaphore = DispatchSemaphore(value: 0)
98	        let box = AgentBox<Result<MediaDescriptor, any Error>>()
99	        MediaImporter.probe(url: url, mayAsk: false) { result in
100	            box.value = result
101	            semaphore.signal()
102	        }
103	        guard semaphore.wait(timeout: .now() + Self.probeCeiling) == .success else {
104	            throw ToolError(message: "Timed out reading \(url.lastPathComponent).")
105	        }
106	        guard let outcome = box.value else {
107	            throw ToolError(message: "Could not read \(url.lastPathComponent).")
108	        }
109	        do {
110	            return try outcome.get()
111	        } catch {
112	            guard let sentence = Self.neverAsksSentence(for: error, url: url) else {
113	                throw ToolError(message: error.localizedDescription)
114	            }
115	            throw ToolError(message: error.localizedDescription + " " + sentence)
116	        }
117	    }
118	
119	    /// What a tool call's refusal adds when an installed ffmpeg could have
120	    /// converted the file but the policy is `ask`, which a call never asks
121	    /// (spec §11 MC-5); nil otherwise. Both refusals that would have gone on
122	    /// to the ffmpeg step count: AVFoundation's (`ImportError`) and, for a
123	    /// WebM or Matroska file, a codec the built-in copy cannot carry
124	    /// (`ContainerRewrapError.unsupported`, spec §11 #216-R).
125	    static func neverAsksSentence(for error: any Error, url: URL) -> String? {
126	        let invites =
127	            (error as? MediaImporter.ImportError)?.invitesFFmpeg
128	            ?? (error as? ContainerRewrapError)?.invitesFFmpeg ?? false
129	        guard invites, !MediaImporter.isImage(url), FFmpegRewrap.policy == .ask,
130	            FFmpegRewrap.tools() != nil
131	        else { return nil }
132	        return "An installed ffmpeg could convert it, but a tool call never asks "
133	            + "(RCFFmpegImport is ask): launch Frame Job with -RCFFmpegImport always, "
134	            + "or import it from the app's window."
135	    }

140	    /// also carries the reasoning for why a caption is a text clip).

142	    /// Runs on the main thread like every other op tool: parsing an SRT is
143	    /// reading a text file, not probing a movie, so there is nothing to wait
144	    /// for and nothing to keep off main.
145	    ///
146	    /// The result reports what was SKIPPED as well as what landed — a
147	    /// caption file with three malformed entries would otherwise import
148	    /// silently short, and a model has no other way to see it.
149	    func importCaptions(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> String {
150	        let document = try target(a)
151	        let path = try requiredString(a, "path")
152	        let url = URL(fileURLWithPath: (path as NSString).expandingTildeInPath)
153	        guard FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: url.path) else {
154	            throw ToolError(message: "No file at \(url.path)")
155	        }
156	        var track: UInt32?
157	        if a["track"] != nil, !(a["track"] is NSNull) {
158	            track = try trackArg(a, "track", document).id
159	        }
160	        let plan: CaptionImporter.Plan
161	        do {
162	            // The EDITED project, like its three siblings (the File-menu
163	            // importer, `Transcriber` and the `transcribe` tool): the ops
164	            // this plan produces are addressed to whatever nest is open, so
165	            // reading the document here would measure a placement against
166	            // the timeline and land the clips inside the nest.
167	            plan = try CaptionImporter.plan(for: url, in: document.editedProject, track: track)
168	        } catch {
169	            throw ToolError(message: error.localizedDescription)
170	        }
171	        var fields: [String: Any] = ["captions": plan.clips, "cues": plan.cues]
172	        if let name = plan.trackName { fields["track_name"] = name }
173	        if plan.trimmed > 0 { fields["trimmed"] = plan.trimmed }
174	        if !plan.problems.isEmpty {
175	            fields["skipped"] = plan.problems.map { $0.description }
176	        }

182	    /// `consolidate_media` — File ▸ Consolidate Media…
183	    /// (`EditorViewController+Consolidate.swift`; `MediaConsolidator` owns
184	    /// the plan, the copying and the four traps).
185	    ///
186	    /// The copy runs on the main thread, where every non-`offMainTools`
187	    /// handler runs: it is `FileManager` work with no waiting in it, so the
188	    /// only cost is that the app's own UI is unresponsive while a large
189	    /// library copies — the connection is served on the server thread and
190	    /// stays live throughout. The app's sheet does the same work on a
191	    /// background queue because there is a person watching that one.
192	    func consolidateMedia(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> String {
193	        let document = try target(a)
194	        let plan: MediaConsolidator.Plan
195	        do {
196	            plan = try MediaConsolidator.plan(for: document)
197	        } catch let error as MediaConsolidator.ConsolidateError {
198	            guard case .untitled = error else {
199	                throw ToolError(message: error.localizedDescription)
200	            }
201	            throw ToolError(
202	                message: error.localizedDescription + " Call save_project with a path first.")
203	        } catch {
204	            throw ToolError(message: error.localizedDescription)
205	        }
206	        // Already self-contained is not an error — it is the state the
207	        // caller asked for, and `editResult` would report the empty op list
208	        // as a refusal.
209	        guard !plan.isEmpty else {
210	            return try jsonResult([
211	                "ok": true, "copied": 0, "directory": plan.directory.path,
212	                "missing": plan.missing,
213	                "note": "Every file this project can find is already inside the package.",
214	                "project": summary(document),
215	            ])
216	        }
217	        let outcome = MediaConsolidator.run(plan)
218	        // Creating `media/` inside the package moves the package's own
219	        // modification date, which NSDocument reads as another application
220	        // having changed the file and refuses every later save over. Told
221	        // unconditionally, since a failed run may still have made it.
222	        document.packageContentsDidChangeOnDisk()
223	        guard !outcome.ops.isEmpty else {
224	            throw ToolError(message: outcome.summary)
225	        }
226	        var fields: [String: Any] = [
227	            "copied": outcome.copied, "bytes": Int(outcome.bytes),
228	            "directory": plan.directory.path, "summary": outcome.summary,
229	        ]
230	        if !outcome.failures.isEmpty { fields["failures"] = outcome.failures }
231	        if !outcome.missing.isEmpty { fields["missing"] = outcome.missing }
232	        let result = try editResult(document, "Consolidate Media", outcome.ops, fields)
233	        document.generateCaches()
234	        return result
235	    }

263	    /// A `media[]` element minus its id, under the model's own key names.
264	    /// Everything but `path` has a default, so a descriptor for a still is
265	    /// `{"path": …, "kind": "image", "width": …, "height": …}`.
266	    private func mediaDescriptor(_ object: [String: Any]) throws -> MediaDescriptor {
267	        let allowed: Set<String> = [
268	            "path", "bookmark", "kind", "duration", "width", "height", "fps", "has_video",
269	            "has_audio", "has_alpha", "original", "color", "cursor",
270	        ]
271	        let unknown = object.keys.filter { !allowed.contains($0) }.sorted()
272	        if let first = unknown.first {
273	            throw ToolError(
274	                message: "Unknown descriptor key \"\(first)\" — allowed keys are "
275	                    + allowed.sorted().joined(separator: ", ") + ".")
276	        }
277	        let path = try requiredString(object, "path")
278	        let kind = try enumArg(object, "kind", MediaKind.self) ?? .video
279	        var fps = Fps.thirty
280	        if let array = object["fps"] as? [Any] {
281	            fps = try fpsPair(array, "descriptor.fps")
282	        } else if object["fps"] != nil, !(object["fps"] is NSNull) {
283	            throw ToolError(
284	                message: "descriptor.fps must be [numerator, denominator], e.g. [30000, 1001].")
285	        }
286	        return MediaDescriptor(
287	            path: (path as NSString).expandingTildeInPath,
288	            bookmark: try stringArg(object, "bookmark"),
289	            kind: kind,
290	            duration: Ticks(try intArg(object, "duration") ?? 0),
291	            width: try intArg(object, "width") ?? 0,
292	            height: try intArg(object, "height") ?? 0,
293	            fps: fps,
294	            hasVideo: try boolArg(object, "has_video") ?? (kind == .video || kind == .image),
295	            hasAudio: try boolArg(object, "has_audio") ?? (kind == .audio),
296	            hasAlpha: try boolArg(object, "has_alpha") ?? false,
297	            original: try mediaOriginal(object["original"]),
298	            color: try mediaColor(object["color"]),
299	            cursor: try mediaCursor(object["cursor"]))
300	    }

305	    /// (`add_media` holds it to `set_media_color`'s rules).

307	        guard let raw = raw, !(raw is NSNull) else { return nil }

309	            throw ToolError(
310	                message: "descriptor.color must be a JSON object {log, gamut?} or {lut} — the "
311	                    + "file's Camera Log, as set_media_color takes it, plus detected — and "
312	                    + "pq, a PQ file's peak as get_project shows it.")
313	        }
314	        let allowed: Set<String> = ["log", "gamut", "lut", "detected", "pq"]
315	        if let first = object.keys.filter({ !allowed.contains($0) }).sorted().first {
316	            throw ToolError(
317	                message: "Unknown color key \"\(first)\" — allowed keys are "
318	                    + allowed.sorted().joined(separator: ", ") + ".")
319	        }
320	        var color = MediaColor(detected: try boolArg(object, "detected") ?? false)
321	        color.log = try enumArg(object, "log", LogCurve.self, label: "descriptor.color.log")
322	        color.gamut = try enumArg(

324	        if object["lut"] != nil, !(object["lut"] is NSNull) {

436	    /// record does not name.

438	        let (document, media) = try onMain {

448	        let descriptor = MediaImporter.relinkProbe(try probe(url), current: media)  // CU-38 (a)
449	        let bookmark = descriptor.path == url.path ? given ?? descriptor.bookmark
450	            : descriptor.bookmark
451	        var fields: [String: Any] = [
452	            "media": Int(media.id), "path": descriptor.path,
453	            "kind": descriptor.kind.rawValue, "duration": descriptor.duration,

455	            "fps": [descriptor.fps.num, descriptor.fps.den],
456	            "has_video": descriptor.hasVideo, "has_audio": descriptor.hasAudio,
457	            "has_alpha": descriptor.hasAlpha,
458	        ]

460	        if let original = descriptor.original { fields["original"] = original.path }

462	            let result = try self.editResult(
463	                document, "Relink Media",
464	                [
465	                    .relinkMedia(
466	                        media: media.id, path: descriptor.path, bookmark: bookmark,
467	                        probe: descriptor)
468	                ],
469	                fields)

//! The two background commands — spec §6's `add_background` and
//! `add_blurred_background` (road map 2, phase 6c).
//!
//! Both answer one question: what goes BEHIND the picture. A 16:10 screen
//! recording on a 16:9 timeline, a phone capture on a landscape canvas, a
//! title standing on nothing — each leaves the canvas showing through, and
//! an editor fills it two ways. A **plate**: a colour, or an image, sized
//! to the canvas. Or a **blurred copy of the clip itself**, blown up past
//! the frame, which is the screencast look — the backdrop is always the
//! right colour because it is made of the same pixels.
//!
//! Both put exactly ONE clip on a NEW track inserted at index 0, the
//! back-most. Not on the back-most EXISTING track: a background is behind
//! everything, and a fresh track is the only place that is true whatever
//! the stack already holds — no overlap to check, nothing already there to
//! push aside, and one undo step to take it all away again. The plate
//! starts at 0 and runs the timeline's length; the blurred copy starts and
//! ends exactly where the clip it copies does.
//!
//! # Why these are core ops
//!
//! The plan of record called Add Blurred Background "a composite over
//! existing ops", and it is worth writing down why it is not, because the
//! recipe it proposed cannot be built and the one that replaces it carries
//! a constraint no single op states.
//!
//! The proposed recipe was the clip's clipboard payload `paste`d onto a new
//! track; that payload carries no `nests` key. (This op refuses a nest clip
//! too, for its own reason — see [`Project::add_blurred_background`] — so
//! that half of the argument is spent and is written down spent rather than
//! left standing.) Re-placing the media with `add_clip`
//! instead loses the SOURCE WINDOW — `add_clip` gives the whole media — so
//! the backdrop of a trimmed clip shows different frames from the

//! The clip and action ops — spec §6, tables "Clips" and "Actions".
//!
//! One `impl Project` block holding clip construction, moves, copies and
//! deletes. Timing edits are in `edit_clip_timing.rs`; their placement commit
//! is in `edit_commit.rs`. The five property patches are the
//! OTHER half of the clip surface, `edit_props.rs`'s, policed by the range
//! checks of `props_check.rs`: this file decides where a clip sits, that one
//! what it looks like. The action ops, which were here, are `edit_action.rs`;
//! the transition ops, which were here too, are `edit_transition.rs`; and
//! `split_clip` with its two helpers, which every splitter in the crate
//! routes through, is `edit_split.rs` — a split is not a placement but a
//! question about what the SECOND clip inherits, and road map 5's E2 added
//! a rule to it. Detach Audio and `set_enabled`, a clip's two halves, are
//! `edit_detach.rs`'s.
//! `edit.rs` dispatches to all of them by name; nothing here knows about JSON
//! op envelopes, and nothing here mutates `self` — an edit clones, changes
//! the clone, and hands it back (spec §5.5).
//!
//! Three rules run through all of it:
//!
//! 1. **Every tick argument is snapped to the canvas frame grid first**
//!    ([`Project::snapped`]), durations included. Nothing sub-frame ever
//!    reaches the model.
//! 2. **Placement is checked, never repaired.** A move, trim or duplicate
//!    that would break the overlap rule is REFUSED, in the rule's own
//!    sentence ([`Outcome::Refused`]) — the UI animates it back. The rule
//!    itself lives in `transition.rs` and is called, never restated, which
//!    is why the sentence the caller reads is the one the rule wrote.
//! 3. **Every op leaves the project valid.** [`Project::finish`] is the
//!    single exit: it answers [`Outcome::Identity`] when the result equals
//!    the input (no phantom undo step) and turns a broken invariant into
//!    `Err`.

107	    pub fn add_background(

124	                let found = self.require_media(id)?.clone();
125	                let has_pixels = found.has_video || matches!(found.kind, MediaKind::Image);

194	    /// Copies `clip` onto a new back-most track, blown up to fill the canvas
195	    /// and blurred — the screencast backdrop (spec §6).
196	    ///
197	    /// The copy keeps the source, the in point, the start, the duration and
198	    /// the speed, so it plays the SAME FRAMES as the clip in front of it and
199	    /// stays exact under any later trim of its own; it drops its audio, its
200	    /// duck, its transition, its actions and its identity, and it takes a
201	    /// fill scale, a centred position, no crop, a `normal` blend and one
202	    /// full-strength blur. The module doc argues each of those.
203	    ///
204	    /// **A NEST clip is refused**, and it is the one refusal here that is
205	    /// not about a missing size — a nest has a frozen canvas and
206	    /// `Project::source_size` answers with it. It is about the BLUR.
207	    /// Flattening
208	    /// (`nest.rs`) folds a nest clip's PLACEMENT down onto the layers inside
209	    /// it and drops every per-pixel property it carries: a nest clip never
210	    /// becomes a layer of its own, so `recipe.rs::layer` reads `filters`,
211	    /// the colour controls, the chroma key, the shadow, the reflection, the
212	    /// spotlight, the hidden regions and the blend off the INNER clip and
213	    /// never off the nest clip. The blur this op writes would therefore
214	    /// reach nothing, and the command would report success having minted a
215	    /// SHARP 1.5× duplicate of the nest sitting behind the original, at
216	    /// double the render cost — a wrong picture answered with no message,
217	    /// which is the failure shape this crate refuses by name everywhere
218	    /// else. It is the same call `edit_props.rs`'s `check_blend` makes about
219	    /// `video.blend` on a nest clip, and `clamp_video`'s about an end patch
220	    /// carrying one; a blur is a per-pixel property like any other. The way
221	    /// in is the round trip the rest of the crate already uses for a nest —
222	    /// ⇧⌘G, blur the clip, ⌘G — and it is what `Frame`'s doc in `nest.rs`
223	    /// records as a limit of the flattening rather than of this op.
224	    ///
225	    /// `Err` for an unknown clip, for a nest, for a source with no pixel
226	    /// size — a text clip, an audio-only one, or a degenerate shape, which
227	    /// have nothing to scale to the canvas — and for a clip carrying no
228	    /// video properties at all. `Err` too when
229	    /// the extra track or clip would break a reader cap, which
230	    /// [`Project::finish`] reports through `validate`. Never an identity: a copy
231	    /// on a new empty track can neither be an identity nor break the overlap
232	    /// rule, so there is nothing here to refuse quietly.
233	    pub fn add_blurred_background(&self, clip: u32) -> Result<Outcome, String> {
234	        let target = self.require_clip(clip)?.clone();
235	        let (mut next, track) = self.with_back_track();
236	        let id = next.allocate_id();
237	        let copy = self.blurred_copy(&target, id, track)?;
238	        next.clips.push(copy);
239	        self.finish(next)
240	    }
241	
242	    /// The blurred copy of `target` with id `id` on track `track`: what
243	    /// [`Project::add_blurred_background`] places, and what `reframe_clip`'s
244	    /// backdrop places (spec §11 VR-25). `Err` for a nest, a source with no
245	    /// pixel size and a clip with no video properties, in that order — the
246	    /// op's own sentences.
247	    pub(crate) fn blurred_copy(&self, target: &Clip, id: u32, track: u32) -> Result<Clip, String> {
248	        let clip = target.id;
249	        if matches!(target.source, Source::Nest { .. }) {
250	            return Err(format!(
251	                "clip {clip} shows a nest, whose own filters the flattening drops, \
252	                 so a blurred copy of it would come out sharp"
253	            ));
254	        }
255	        let Some((source_width, source_height)) = self.source_size(target) else {
256	            return Err(format!(
257	                "clip {clip}'s source has no pixel size, so nothing can be scaled to fill the canvas"
258	            ));
259	        };
260	        let Some(video) = target.video.clone() else {
261	            return Err(format!("clip {clip} has no video properties"));
262	        };
263	
264	        let mut copy = target.clone();
265	        copy.id = id;
266	        copy.track = track;
267	        // The pair `detach_audio` sets, read the other way: this half of the
268	        // clip is the picture, and the sound stays with the original.
269	        copy.enabled = Enabled {
270	            video: true,
271	            audio: false,
272	        };
273	        // The one field of the audio group that is not about this clip's own
274	        // sound. `duckers` gathers a duck from the flattened timeline with no
275	        // test of `enabled.audio`, a mute or a solo, so a copy that kept one
276	        // would duck the whole mix — the clip it was copied from included,
277	        // since the copy is a voice on no track and the `others` filter has
278	        // nothing to exclude it by. A picture command may not change the
279	        // sound, and no rendered frame could catch it if it did.
280	        copy.audio = copy.audio.map(|audio| AudioProps {
281	            duck: None,
282	            ..audio
283	        });
284	        copy.transition_in = None;
285	        copy.actions = Vec::new();
286	        copy.name = Some(BLURRED_BACKGROUND_NAME.to_string());
287	        copy.label = None;
288	        copy.video = Some(VideoProps {
289	            scale: self.fill_scale(source_width, source_height),
290	            x: 0.0,
291	            y: 0.0,
292	            crop: Crop::default(),
293	            filters: vec![Filter {
294	                kind: FilterKind::Blur,
295	                amount: 1.0,
296	            }],
297	            // A plate composites with the CANVAS, never with a mode chosen
298	            // for the picture in front of it — over the default black that
299	            // mode is either destructive or inert. The module doc argues it.
300	            blend: BlendMode::Normal,
301	            // And it does not MOVE (format version 8). A backdrop that slid
302	            // in, spun or pulsed behind the clip it was copied from would
303	            // be two pictures of one recording disagreeing about where they
304	            // are, which is the visible half of the same mistake as keeping
305	            // the audio switch — and a slide would leave the canvas showing
306	            // down one side, which is the one thing a background exists to
307	            // prevent.
308	            motion: None,
309	            // A backdrop cut down to the person is no backdrop (CO-20).
310	            cutout: None,
311	            // Nor is one cut by the person in front of it (CO-52).
312	            behind_subject: false,
313	            // Drawn behind and sharp, so it drops the blur (CU-113).
314	            motion_blur: 0.0,
315	            ..video
316	        });
317	        Ok(copy)
318	    }
319	}

321	    /// Checks the overlap rule against the state `track` would be left in.
322	    ///
323	    /// `candidates` are the clips in their PROPOSED positions (a move's
324	    /// destinations, a trim's result, a new clip); `ignore` lists clip ids
325	    /// to treat as absent, which is how a move removes the clips from where
326	    /// they were. A candidate's own id is ignored too, so a caller that
327	    /// forgets `ignore` still gets the right answer instead of a clip
328	    /// colliding with itself. Candidates for other tracks are skipped, so a
329	    /// multi-track move can pass the whole set to each destination track.
330	    ///
331	    /// The check is over the WHOLE resulting track, not just around the
332	    /// candidates: the rule is an invariant of the track, and the plan's
333	    /// A/B assignment (spec §7.2, at most two composition tracks per
334	    /// timeline track) depends on it holding everywhere.
335	    ///
336	    /// `Ok(())` or an `Err` naming the first violation, which the calling
337	    /// op hands straight on as its refusal — `Outcome::Refused` carrying
338	    /// THIS sentence, `reason_out` at the FFI, an animate-back in the UI.
339	    /// The rule is therefore written once: the clip ids and the tick counts
340	    /// a caller acts on are the ones computed here.
341	    pub fn check_overlap_rule(
342	        &self,
343	        candidates: &[Clip],
344	        track: u32,
345	        ignore: &[u32],
346	    ) -> Result<(), String> {
347	        let mut placed: Vec<&Clip> = self
348	            .clips
349	            .iter()
350	            .filter(|c| {
351	                c.track == track
352	                    && !ignore.contains(&c.id)
353	                    && !candidates.iter().any(|k| k.id == c.id)
354	            })
355	            .collect();
356	        placed.extend(candidates.iter().filter(|c| c.track == track));
357	        placed.sort_by_key(|c| (c.start, c.id));
358	
359	        for i in 0..placed.len() {
360	            if let (Some(a), Some(b)) = (placed.get(i), placed.get(i + 1)) {
361	                if let Some(overlap) = overlap_of(a, b) {
362	                    // No overlap may hold an adjustment clip (spec §11
363	                    // GR-6): it cannot take the transition an overlap is.
364	                    if let Some(why) = adjustment_overlap(a, b) {
365	                        return Err(why);
366	                    }
367	                    // Half of the SHORTER clip. Integer halving truncates,
368	                    // which errs toward refusing — the safe side, since an
369	                    // over-long overlap is what breaks the A/B assignment.
370	                    let limit = overlap_limit(a, b);
371	                    if overlap.duration > limit {
372	                        return Err(format!(
373	                            "clips {} and {} would overlap by {} ticks, more than half of the \
374	                             shorter clip ({} ticks)",
375	                            a.id, b.id, overlap.duration, limit
376	                        ));
377	                    }
378	                }
379	            }
380	            // Clips are in start order, so a clip that reaches any
381	            // non-adjacent clip necessarily reaches the one two along:
382	            // testing i and i+2 catches every "two neighbours on one side"
383	            // case in a single linear pass.
384	            if let (Some(a), Some(b), Some(c)) =
385	                (placed.get(i), placed.get(i + 1), placed.get(i + 2))
386	            {
387	                if overlap_of(a, c).is_some() {
388	                    return Err(format!(
389	                        "clip {} would overlap more than one neighbour on one side \
390	                         (clips {} and {})",
391	                        a.id, b.id, c.id
392	                    ));
393	                }
394	            }
395	        }
396	        Ok(())
397	    }
398	}

437	impl Project {
438	    /// Moves the clip's start edge to `to`, advancing the source in point
439	    /// by `(to - start) × speed` so the frame under the edge does not move
440	    /// (spec §6).
441	    ///
442	    /// Clamped to the source bound — `to ≥ start - in/speed` snapped UP to
443	    /// a frame, `source_window.rs`'s `earliest_start_on_grid` (spec §11,
444	    /// D4-5) — and to leaving at least one frame of clip. Actions are
445	    /// deliberately left alone: clip-relative, rebasing would drop or bake
446	    /// whatever fell off the front, which is lossy and makes trimming back
447	    /// out not an identity. On a RAMPED clip the actions keep their clip
448	    /// time too, so `in` advances by round(S(Δ)) moving in and at the base
449	    /// rate moving out, and the edge is held where the clip still fits its
450	    /// media (`front_edge_held`, spec §11 SR-18 (c)): what plays after the
451	    /// new start can change. `text.words` are the opposite, on purpose
452	    /// (spec §11, W-3): a word is anchored to speech that stays where it is
453	    /// on the timeline, so every word is rebased by the trim's delta and a
454	    /// word trimmed off the front keeps its (negative) time. A graphic's
455	    /// `in` advances by the same delta (road map 10's G-9), with no speed
456	    /// and no head bound, never below 0.
457	    ///
458	    /// Without `alone`, a linked partner whose start is this clip's is
459	    /// trimmed to the same `to` after it, by its own clamps; with it, the
460	    /// clip moves alone — the J-cut (spec §11 AU-93, `carried_edge`).
461	    pub fn trim_start(&self, clip: u32, to: Ticks, alone: bool) -> Result<Outcome, String> {
462	        self.carried_edge(
463	            clip,
464	            alone,
465	            |target, partner| partner.start == target.start,
466	            |project, id| project.trim_start_one(id, to),
467	        )
468	    }
469	
470	    fn trim_start_one(&self, clip: u32, to: Ticks) -> Result<Outcome, String> {
471	        let target = self.require_clip(clip)?.clone();
472	        let end = clip_end(&target);
473	        let latest = end.saturating_sub(self.frame());
474	        let mut to = self.snapped(to).min(latest).max(0);
475

483	        // in front: then there is no legal new start, so nothing happens.
484	        if to > latest || to == target.start {
485	            return Ok(Outcome::Identity);
486	        }

489	        let mut moved = target.clone();

491	        moved.start = to;

536	    /// source range it shows: `speed = source_len / (to_end - start)`
537	    /// (spec §6). Media sources only.
538	    ///
539	    /// An IDENTITY when the new length is under a frame or the resulting rate
540	    /// falls outside `SPEED_MIN`–`SPEED_MAX`; refused only when the placement
541	    /// breaks the overlap rule. Actions keep their clip-relative fraction.
542	    ///
543	    /// On a RAMPED clip the whole rate profile scales by f = D ÷ (to_end −
544	    /// start) through `scaled_profile`, so the ramp keeps its shape and its
545	    /// window; an f that would take any rate the clip names past the limits
546	    /// (`profile_factors`) changes nothing (spec §11 SR-19 (a), (b)).
547	    /// Refused on a linked clip (spec §11 AU-94).
548	    pub fn rate_stretch(&self, clip: u32, to_end: Ticks) -> Result<Outcome, String> {
549	        let target = self.require_clip(clip)?.clone();
550	        if !matches!(target.source, Source::Media { .. }) {
551	            return Err(format!("clip {clip} is not a media clip"));
552	        }
553	        let to_end = self.snapped(to_end);
554	        let duration = to_end.saturating_sub(target.start);
555	        if duration < self.frame() {
556	            return Ok(Outcome::Identity);
557	        }
558	        if let Some((low, high)) = profile_factors(&target) {
559	            let factor = target.duration as f64 / duration as f64;
560	            if !factor.is_finite() || !(low..=high).contains(&factor) {
561	                return Ok(Outcome::Identity);
562	            }
563	            let moved = self.scaled_profile(&target, factor, duration);
564	            return self.commit_rate(&target, moved);
565	        }
566	        let rate = self.content_length_in_source(&target) as f64 / duration as f64;
567	        if !rate.is_finite() || !(SPEED_MIN..=SPEED_MAX).contains(&rate) {
568	            return Ok(Outcome::Identity);
569	        }
570	
571	        let mut moved = target.clone();
572	        moved.speed = rate;
573	        moved.duration = duration;
574	        self.rescale_actions(&mut moved.actions, target.duration, duration);
575	        self.commit_rate(&target, moved)
576	    }

77	    /// `add_clip` takes a Fit one — the module doc argues that one

80	    /// at scale 1 — the rectangle IS the canvas, so there is nothing for

88	    /// `set_shape` after it.

91	    /// caller that named both meant one of them), for an unknown media, for
92	    /// a media with no pictures to show, for a colour outside 0–1, and for a
93	    /// duration under a frame — and, through [`Project::finish`], when the
94	    /// extra track or clip would break a reader cap. Never an identity: the clip
95	    /// lands on a track of its own, so there is nothing here to refuse
96	    /// quietly.
