99	    /// whether the duration was given or defaulted to the timeline's (spec
100	    /// §11, D4-4). It reads [`Project::whole_media_length`], which is what
101	    /// `add_clip` gives a clip of the same file, so the plate ends where
102	    /// its file does and its segment plays at rate 1. What that paragraph
103	    /// used to say — that an unclamped plate "shows nothing" past the end
104	    /// of its media — was measured FALSE: the plan stretched a six-second
105	    /// file over a twelve-second plate at rate 0.5. An image plate is
106	    /// unclamped still, having no source bound at all.
107	    pub fn add_background(
108	        &self,
109	        media: Option<u32>,
110	        color: Option<Color>,
111	        duration: Option<Ticks>,
112	    ) -> Result<Outcome, String> {
113	        if let (Some(media), Some(_)) = (media, color) {
114	            return Err(format!(
115	                "add_background takes a media or a color, not both (media {media})"
116	            ));
117	        }
118	        let mut duration = self.plate_duration(duration)?;
119	
120	        // Everything that can refuse is decided against `self`, before a
121	        // track exists to leave behind.
122	        let (source, video, audio, shape) = match media {
123	            Some(id) => {
124	                let found = self.require_media(id)?.clone();
125	                let has_pixels = found.has_video || matches!(found.kind, MediaKind::Image);
126	                if !(has_pixels && found.width > 0 && found.height > 0) {
127	                    return Err(format!(
128	                        "media {id} has no pixel size, so it cannot be a background"
129	                    ));
130	                }
131	                let source = match found.kind {
132	                    MediaKind::Image => Source::Image { media: id },
133	                    MediaKind::Video | MediaKind::Audio => {
134	                        // A timed plate is held INSIDE its own file, by the
135	                        // same function `add_clip` measures a whole media
136	                        // with — so the plate's two `Err` sentences are
137	                        // that op's, and the segment plays at rate 1
138	                        // (spec §11, D4-4).
139	                        duration = duration.min(self.whole_media_length(&found)?);
140	                        Source::Media {
141	                            media: id,
142	                            r#in: 0,
143	                            reversed: false,
144	                        }
145	                    }
146	                    // Unreached: a LUT's row has no pixels, refused above.
147	                    MediaKind::Lut => return Err(crate::lut::lut_not_placeable(id)),
148	                };
149	                // FILL, not `add_clip`'s Fit: a plate that leaves the canvas
150	                // showing down one side has failed at the one thing a
151	                // background is for, and whether Fit leaves it showing
152	                // depends on `canvas.fit_new_clips`, which has no opinion
153	                // about backgrounds. The module doc argues it at length.
154	                let video = VideoProps {
155	                    scale: self.fill_scale(f64::from(found.width), f64::from(found.height)),
156	                    ..VideoProps::default()
157	                };
158	                (
159	                    source,
160	                    video,
161	                    found.has_audio.then(AudioProps::default),
162	                    None,
163	                )
164	            }
165	            None => {
166	                let plate = ShapeProps {
167	                    kind: ShapeKind::Rectangle,
168	                    width: f64::from(self.canvas.width),
169	                    height: f64::from(self.canvas.height),
170	                    stroke: None,
171	                    fill: Some(color.unwrap_or(DEFAULT_PLATE)),
172	                    ..ShapeProps::default()
173	                };
174	                // The caller's colour reaches the same check a `set_shape`
175	                // of it would, so `[0, 0, 255, 1]` is named here rather
176	                // than blown out on the canvas.
177	                check_shape(&plate)?;
178	                (Source::Shape, VideoProps::default(), None, Some(plate))
179	            }
180	        };
181	
182	        let (mut next, track) = self.with_back_track();
183	        let clip = Clip {
184	            video: Some(video),
185	            audio,
186	            shape,
187	            name: Some(BACKGROUND_NAME.to_string()),
188	            ..Clip::placed(next.allocate_id(), track, 0, duration, source)
189	        };
190	        next.clips.push(clip);
191	        self.finish(next)
192	    }

194	    /// Copies `clip` onto a new back-most track, blown up to fill the canvas
195	    /// and blurred — the screencast backdrop (spec §6).
196	    ///
197	    /// The copy keeps the source, the in point, the start, the duration and
198	    /// the speed, so it plays the SAME FRAMES as the clip in front of it and
199	    /// stays exact under any later trim of its own; it drops its audio, its
200	    /// duck, its transition, its actions and its identity, and it takes a
201	    /// fill scale, a centred position, no crop, a `normal` blend and one
202	    /// full-strength blur. The module doc argues each of those.
203	    ///
204	    /// **A NEST clip is refused**, and it is the one refusal here that is
205	    /// not about a missing size — a nest has a frozen canvas and
206	    /// `Project::source_size` answers with it. It is about the BLUR.
207	    /// Flattening
208	    /// (`nest.rs`) folds a nest clip's PLACEMENT down onto the layers inside
209	    /// it and drops every per-pixel property it carries: a nest clip never
210	    /// becomes a layer of its own, so `recipe.rs::layer` reads `filters`,
211	    /// the colour controls, the chroma key, the shadow, the reflection, the
212	    /// spotlight, the hidden regions and the blend off the INNER clip and
213	    /// never off the nest clip. The blur this op writes would therefore
214	    /// reach nothing, and the command would report success having minted a
215	    /// SHARP 1.5× duplicate of the nest sitting behind the original, at
216	    /// double the render cost — a wrong picture answered with no message,
217	    /// which is the failure shape this crate refuses by name everywhere
218	    /// else. It is the same call `edit_props.rs`'s `check_blend` makes about
219	    /// `video.blend` on a nest clip, and `clamp_video`'s about an end patch
220	    /// carrying one; a blur is a per-pixel property like any other. The way
221	    /// in is the round trip the rest of the crate already uses for a nest —
222	    /// ⇧⌘G, blur the clip, ⌘G — and it is what `Frame`'s doc in `nest.rs`
223	    /// records as a limit of the flattening rather than of this op.
224	    ///
225	    /// `Err` for an unknown clip, for a nest, for a source with no pixel
226	    /// size — a text clip, an audio-only one, or a degenerate shape, which
227	    /// have nothing to scale to the canvas — and for a clip carrying no
228	    /// video properties at all. `Err` too when
229	    /// the extra track or clip would break a reader cap, which
230	    /// [`Project::finish`] reports through `validate`. Never an identity: a copy
231	    /// on a new empty track can neither be an identity nor break the overlap
232	    /// rule, so there is nothing here to refuse quietly.
233	    pub fn add_blurred_background(&self, clip: u32) -> Result<Outcome, String> {
234	        let target = self.require_clip(clip)?.clone();
235	        let (mut next, track) = self.with_back_track();
236	        let id = next.allocate_id();
237	        let copy = self.blurred_copy(&target, id, track)?;
238	        next.clips.push(copy);
239	        self.finish(next)
240	    }

242	    /// The blurred copy of `target` with id `id` on track `track`: what
243	    /// [`Project::add_blurred_background`] places, and what `reframe_clip`'s
244	    /// backdrop places (spec §11 VR-25). `Err` for a nest, a source with no
245	    /// pixel size and a clip with no video properties, in that order — the
246	    /// op's own sentences.
247	    pub(crate) fn blurred_copy(&self, target: &Clip, id: u32, track: u32) -> Result<Clip, String> {
248	        let clip = target.id;
249	        if matches!(target.source, Source::Nest { .. }) {
250	            return Err(format!(
251	                "clip {clip} shows a nest, whose own filters the flattening drops, \
252	                 so a blurred copy of it would come out sharp"
253	            ));
254	        }
255	        let Some((source_width, source_height)) = self.source_size(target) else {
256	            return Err(format!(
257	                "clip {clip}'s source has no pixel size, so nothing can be scaled to fill the canvas"
258	            ));
259	        };
260	        let Some(video) = target.video.clone() else {
261	            return Err(format!("clip {clip} has no video properties"));
262	        };
263	
264	        let mut copy = target.clone();
265	        copy.id = id;
266	        copy.track = track;
267	        // The pair `detach_audio` sets, read the other way: this half of the
268	        // clip is the picture, and the sound stays with the original.
269	        copy.enabled = Enabled {
270	            video: true,
271	            audio: false,
272	        };
273	        // The one field of the audio group that is not about this clip's own
274	        // sound. `duckers` gathers a duck from the flattened timeline with no
275	        // test of `enabled.audio`, a mute or a solo, so a copy that kept one
276	        // would duck the whole mix — the clip it was copied from included,
277	        // since the copy is a voice on no track and the `others` filter has
278	        // nothing to exclude it by. A picture command may not change the
279	        // sound, and no rendered frame could catch it if it did.
280	        copy.audio = copy.audio.map(|audio| AudioProps {
281	            duck: None,
282	            ..audio
283	        });
284	        copy.transition_in = None;
285	        copy.actions = Vec::new();
286	        copy.name = Some(BLURRED_BACKGROUND_NAME.to_string());
287	        copy.label = None;
288	        copy.video = Some(VideoProps {
289	            scale: self.fill_scale(source_width, source_height),
290	            x: 0.0,
291	            y: 0.0,
292	            crop: Crop::default(),
293	            filters: vec![Filter {
294	                kind: FilterKind::Blur,
295	                amount: 1.0,
296	            }],
297	            // A plate composites with the CANVAS, never with a mode chosen
298	            // for the picture in front of it — over the default black that
299	            // mode is either destructive or inert. The module doc argues it.
300	            blend: BlendMode::Normal,
301	            // And it does not MOVE (format version 8). A backdrop that slid
302	            // in, spun or pulsed behind the clip it was copied from would
303	            // be two pictures of one recording disagreeing about where they
304	            // are, which is the visible half of the same mistake as keeping
305	            // the audio switch — and a slide would leave the canvas showing
306	            // down one side, which is the one thing a background exists to
307	            // prevent.
308	            motion: None,
309	            // A backdrop cut down to the person is no backdrop (CO-20).
310	            cutout: None,
311	            // Nor is one cut by the person in front of it (CO-52).
312	            behind_subject: false,
313	            // Drawn behind and sharp, so it drops the blur (CU-113).
314	            motion_blur: 0.0,
315	            ..video
316	        });
317	        Ok(copy)
318	    }

321	    /// Checks the overlap rule against the state `track` would be left in.
322	    ///
323	    /// `candidates` are the clips in their PROPOSED positions (a move's
324	    /// destinations, a trim's result, a new clip); `ignore` lists clip ids
325	    /// to treat as absent, which is how a move removes the clips from where
326	    /// they were. A candidate's own id is ignored too, so a caller that
327	    /// forgets `ignore` still gets the right answer instead of a clip
328	    /// colliding with itself. Candidates for other tracks are skipped, so a
329	    /// multi-track move can pass the whole set to each destination track.
330	    ///
331	    /// The check is over the WHOLE resulting track, not just around the
332	    /// candidates: the rule is an invariant of the track, and the plan's
333	    /// A/B assignment (spec §7.2, at most two composition tracks per
334	    /// timeline track) depends on it holding everywhere.
335	    ///
336	    /// `Ok(())` or an `Err` naming the first violation, which the calling
337	    /// op hands straight on as its refusal — `Outcome::Refused` carrying
338	    /// THIS sentence, `reason_out` at the FFI, an animate-back in the UI.
339	    /// The rule is therefore written once: the clip ids and the tick counts
340	    /// a caller acts on are the ones computed here.
341	    pub fn check_overlap_rule(
342	        &self,
343	        candidates: &[Clip],
344	        track: u32,
345	        ignore: &[u32],
346	    ) -> Result<(), String> {
347	        let mut placed: Vec<&Clip> = self
348	            .clips
349	            .iter()
350	            .filter(|c| {
351	                c.track == track
352	                    && !ignore.contains(&c.id)
353	                    && !candidates.iter().any(|k| k.id == c.id)
354	            })
355	            .collect();
356	        placed.extend(candidates.iter().filter(|c| c.track == track));
357	        placed.sort_by_key(|c| (c.start, c.id));
358	
359	        for i in 0..placed.len() {
360	            if let (Some(a), Some(b)) = (placed.get(i), placed.get(i + 1)) {
361	                if let Some(overlap) = overlap_of(a, b) {
362	                    // No overlap may hold an adjustment clip (spec §11
363	                    // GR-6): it cannot take the transition an overlap is.
364	                    if let Some(why) = adjustment_overlap(a, b) {
365	                        return Err(why);
366	                    }
367	                    // Half of the SHORTER clip. Integer halving truncates,
368	                    // which errs toward refusing — the safe side, since an
369	                    // over-long overlap is what breaks the A/B assignment.
370	                    let limit = overlap_limit(a, b);
371	                    if overlap.duration > limit {
372	                        return Err(format!(
373	                            "clips {} and {} would overlap by {} ticks, more than half of the \
374	                             shorter clip ({} ticks)",
375	                            a.id, b.id, overlap.duration, limit
376	                        ));
377	                    }
378	                }
379	            }
380	            // Clips are in start order, so a clip that reaches any
381	            // non-adjacent clip necessarily reaches the one two along:
382	            // testing i and i+2 catches every "two neighbours on one side"
383	            // case in a single linear pass.
384	            if let (Some(a), Some(b), Some(c)) =
385	                (placed.get(i), placed.get(i + 1), placed.get(i + 2))
386	            {
387	                if overlap_of(a, c).is_some() {
388	                    return Err(format!(
389	                        "clip {} would overlap more than one neighbour on one side \
390	                         (clips {} and {})",
391	                        a.id, b.id, c.id
392	                    ));
393	                }
394	            }
395	        }
396	        Ok(())
397	    }

import Foundation

// MARK: - What the assistant may not call, and what it asks about first

/// Spec §11 AI-7 as ONE table: every tool the assistant may not call
/// (`withheld`) or must ask the person about first (`askFirst`), each row with
/// its reason. The lane reads it (`AgentLane.submit`); an MCP caller never
/// does, because the rule belongs to the assistant's lane and not to the tool.
enum AssistantToolRule {
    case withheld
    case askFirst
}

/// One row. `onlyWith` narrows the row to calls carrying that argument with
/// that string value (`transcribe` is withheld only for the cloud engine).
/// `askOnlyWith` narrows an ask-first row to calls carrying that argument
/// (`new_project_from_range` asks only when it names `path`, CJ-52); declared
/// last, with a default, so every other row's init is unchanged.
struct AssistantToolRow {
    let tool: String
    let rule: AssistantToolRule
    let onlyWith: (key: String, value: String)?
    let reason: String
    var askOnlyWith: String? = nil
}

/// What the person is asked before an ask-first tool runs: the tool, where it
/// writes, and whether something is already there.
struct AssistantQuestion {
    let tool: String
    let path: String?
    let exists: Bool

    /// "export writes <path>", "export REPLACES <path>" when a file is already
    /// there (A0 E2: `export` replaces without asking), "<tool> writes a file"
    /// with no path; `consolidate_media` says what it copies, and where.
    var sentence: String {
        if tool == "consolidate_media" {
            return "consolidate_media copies every referenced file into "
                + (path ?? "the project's package")
        }
        guard let path = path else { return "\(tool) writes a file" }
        return exists ? "\(tool) REPLACES \(path)" : "\(tool) writes \(path)"
    }
}

enum AssistantToolTable {
    /// The product tools the table names. The dev tools are withheld too, by
    /// `row(for:)`, from `AgentServer.devToolNames`, so a new dev tool needs no
    /// row here.
    static let rows: [AssistantToolRow] = [
        AssistantToolRow(
            tool: "record_screen", rule: .withheld, onlyWith: nil,
            reason: "Recording is a person at the Record button (File ▸ New Recording…)."),
        AssistantToolRow(
            tool: "close_project", rule: .withheld, onlyWith: nil,
            reason: "Closing a project closes the window this conversation lives in (AI-5); the "
                + "person closes it with File ▸ Close (⌘W)."),
        AssistantToolRow(
            tool: "transcribe", rule: .withheld, onlyWith: (key: "engine", value: "assemblyai"),
            reason: "Audio leaves the machine only by name, with the price in front of the "
                + "person (spec §11 R6-2). Use File ▸ Generate Captions…, which shows what is "
                + "uploaded and what it costs."),
        AssistantToolRow(
            tool: "transcribe_for_fillers", rule: .withheld, onlyWith: nil,
            reason: "Audio leaves the machine only by name, with the price in front of the "
                + "person (spec §11 R6-2). Use Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words…, which shows what is "
                + "uploaded and what it costs."),
        AssistantToolRow(
            tool: "export", rule: .askFirst, onlyWith: nil,
            reason: "It writes a movie where the model chose, replacing any file already there "
                + "(A0 E2)."),
        AssistantToolRow(
            tool: "export_captions", rule: .askFirst, onlyWith: nil,
            reason: "It writes a caption file."),
        AssistantToolRow(
            tool: "save_project", rule: .askFirst, onlyWith: nil,
            reason: "It writes the package."),
        AssistantToolRow(
            tool: "consolidate_media", rule: .askFirst, onlyWith: nil,
            reason: "It copies every referenced file into the package."),
        AssistantToolRow(
            tool: "export_graphic", rule: .askFirst, onlyWith: nil,
            reason: "It writes a .fjgraphic package where the model chose, replacing any file "
                + "already there."),
        AssistantToolRow(
            tool: "new_project_from_range", rule: .askFirst, onlyWith: nil,
            reason: "It writes a project package where the model chose, when the call names a "
                + "path.",
            askOnlyWith: "path"),
        AssistantToolRow(
            tool: "make_vertical_version", rule: .askFirst, onlyWith: nil,
            reason: "It writes a project package where the model chose, when the call names a "
                + "path.",
            askOnlyWith: "path"),
    ]

    static let devToolReason =
        "a developer tool (spec §11 V-1): Distribution has none, and the assistant sees one "
        + "catalog in both builds."

    /// The row governing `tool`: every dev tool is withheld (V-1), else the
    /// table's own row, else nil (the tool is the assistant's to call).
    static func row(for tool: String) -> AssistantToolRow? {
        if AgentServer.devToolNames.contains(tool) {
            return AssistantToolRow(
                tool: tool, rule: .withheld, onlyWith: nil, reason: devToolReason)
        }
        return rows.first { $0.tool == tool }
    }

title: Duck by Speech
description: Lower the other clips only while this clip's speech plays, so the music comes back up in the pauses.

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Duck by Speech lowers the other clips only around this clip's stretches of speech, so the music rises again when the voice stops. It's [Ducking](/audio/ducking/) with **Duck by** set to **Speech**.

<AtAGlance
  where="Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Ducking ▸ Duck by"
  tools={['set_audio', 'set_media_speech']}
  needs="Nothing. Speech is detected on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
/>

## Duck only while someone speaks

<Steps>

1. Select the voice clip and open the **Sound** sub-tab of the Clip tab.

2. In the **Ducking** section, tick **Duck other audio**.

3. Set **Duck by** to **Speech**.

4. Adjust [Pre-roll and Hold](#set-pre-roll-and-hold) if the music moves too early or too late.

</Steps>
